a_rows_sample.anchor: Finding 2 — a false birth caught, and P-97 corroborated at census scale ... It is a regex defect. ... P-97 CORROBORATED — and now at census scale, not queue scale. ... Rule adopted: every birth-census pattern is word-bounded, and every earliest hit is read before it is recorded.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reports catching and correcting its own false-birth error: an initial census pass placed Sat's earliest occurrence at step-008 (2026-08-27 15:19:20), 66 minutes before step_023 (the previously-established P-97 birth point), which would have refuted P-97 -- traced to a regex matching the tail of a different object (IdealSatisfied(P)) for lack of a word boundary. With a word boundary, step_023 (16:25:45) is confirmed as the true earliest across all nine lanes, corroborating P-97 at census scale. Notes this is the third instance of the same token-birth-vs-object-birth trap in this programme (after Adequacy/Standing and the Sanskrit 'Sat'), and adopts a standing methodological rule: every birth-census pattern must be word-bounded, and every earliest hit must be read before being recorded.

b_rows_sample.anchor: O\rightarrow E\rightarrow Q\rightarrow I\rightarrow K and K\rightarrow D\rightarrow A.
b_rows_sample.statement: First correction: a single set K cannot mean 'knowledge' generically -- distinguishes O (Observation), E (Evidence), Q (Claim), I (Inference), K (Accepted Knowledge), D (Decision), A (Action) as different domain objects, giving epistemic progression O->E->Q->I->K and operational progression K->D->A.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Role(X,C) determines its domain meaning in context C. ... Artifact\neq EpistemicRole. Meaning is contextual.
b_rows_sample.statement: Artifact versus epistemic role: for artifact X, Role(X,C) determines its domain meaning in context C, so Artifact != EpistemicRole -- the same artifact can be evidence in one context and historical knowledge after acceptance in another; 'meaning is contextual' connects DDD directly to the mathematical model.

b_rows_sample.anchor: C=(S_C,V_C,R_C,P_C,A_C)
b_rows_sample.statement: Context is formalized beyond a bounded-context name as a 5-tuple C=(S_C semantic vocabulary, V_C validity rules, R_C material distinctions, P_C policies, A_C authority model) -- a DDD bounded context is thus a semantic and governance environment.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \llbracket x\rrbracket_{C_1}\neq\llbracket x\rrbracket_{C_2}. Same representation \not\Rightarrow same meaning.
b_rows_sample.statement: Bounded context as semantic space: an object x has meaning through a context-relative denotation [[x]]_C, and the same representation can have different meanings under different contexts ([[x]]_C1 != [[x]]_C2) -- 'same representation does not imply same meaning' is proposed as a mathematical foundation of DDD bounded contexts.

b_rows_sample.anchor: x_1\sim_\phi x_2\iff\phi(x_1)=\phi(x_2). ... [x]_\phi.
b_rows_sample.statement: Context mapping phi_AB: S_A -> S_B between bounded contexts is not assumed bijective (often partial/many-to-one/one-to-many/conditional/lossy); it induces an equivalence relation x1 ~phi x2 iff phi(x1)=phi(x2) with equivalence classes [x]_phi, giving a rigorous formal handle on information/semantic collapse.

b_rows_sample.anchor: SemanticViolation\iff MaterialDistinction\land UncontrolledCollapse.
b_rows_sample.statement: Semantic loss is formalized precisely: a collapse phi_AB(x1)=phi_AB(x2) where x1 is not~_A x2 is a candidate semantic-loss event, but is an error (SemanticViolation) only if the collapsed distinction belongs to R_A or R_B (i.e. is material) -- SemanticViolation iff MaterialDistinction and UncontrolledCollapse, much stronger than simply 'preserve semantics'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: M_A(x_1,x_2)\land\phi(x_1)=\phi(x_2)\Rightarrow DeclaredLoss
b_rows_sample.statement: Context-specific materiality predicate M_C(x1,x2) ('the distinction between x1 and x2 is material in context C') yields the architectural invariant candidate: M_A(x1,x2) and phi(x1)=phi(x2) implies DeclaredLoss for a transformation crossing from A to B.

b_rows_sample.anchor: T=(K_A,C_A,A_t,P_t,E_t,\tau)\rightarrow(K_B,C_B).
b_rows_sample.statement: Transformation T is progressively enriched from a bare (K_A,C_A)->(K_B,C_B) mapping to a full domain operation T=(K_A,C_A,Actor_t,Policy_t,Evidence_t,tau)->(K_B,C_B), with the DDD distinction Command (expresses intent) -> Transformation (domain operation/process) -> Event (records what happened).

b_rows_sample.anchor: L(K_t)=\{(K_i,T_i,A_i,E_i,\tau_i,C_i)\}. ... KnowledgeOS lineage = typed provenance graph.
b_rows_sample.statement: Lineage is formalized as a typed provenance graph G_L=(V_L,E_L) (nodes=knowledge states/artifacts, edges=transformations carrying metadata (T,A,E,C,tau)), generally a DAG allowing branching (K1->{K2^A,K2^B}) and merging -- substantially stronger than an ordinary version chain.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Auth(a,r,c,p) mean actor a is authorized under role r, context c, and policy p. ... Identity\neq Authority.
b_rows_sample.statement: Authority is formalized as a relation Auth(a,r,c,p) (actor, role, context, policy) rather than A=User; an action is legitimate only if Auth(a,r,c,p)=True, giving Identity != Authority (authenticated but not authorized is possible).

b_rows_sample.anchor: E_q=(source,observation,context,time,method,provenance). ... E_q\xrightarrow{\mathcal I}Q.
b_rows_sample.statement: Evidence is formalized as a 6-tuple E_q=(source,observation,context,time,method,provenance) rather than a boolean Evidence=True, supporting a claim Q via an inferential procedure E_q -I-> Q.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \hat F_n\neq F. Observation\neq PopulationTruth.
b_rows_sample.statement: Statistical interpretation of evidence: the empirical distribution hat F_n(x) estimates but is not identical to the underlying distribution F, giving Observation != PopulationTruth; likewise a confidence interval must never be silently converted into a ProbabilityOfTruth.

b_rows_sample.anchor: P(\theta\mid E)=\frac{P(E\mid\theta)P(\theta)}{P(E)}. ... Bayesian machinery is one possible formalism for representing uncertainty where the domain permits probabilistic interpretation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Bayesian evidence via Bayes' rule is offered as one possible uncertainty formalism, not a mandatory commitment -- must not be introduced merely because 'KnowledgeOS is probabilistic'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Assurance=DeterministicAssurance\cup StatisticalEvidence\cup HumanJudgement.
b_rows_sample.statement: Two assurance modes are distinguished and must not be conflated: Deterministic (I(x)=True/False, e.g. SchemaValid(x)) and Statistical (P(H|E) or an estimator with uncertainty), together with human judgment forming Assurance = DeterministicAssurance union StatisticalEvidence union HumanJudgement; the appropriate mode depends on the invariant.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Hash(x)=h. ... P(X>x). ... Meaning(x,C). ... Authorized(a,p). These require different mathematical structures.
b_rows_sample.statement: Architectural properties are classified by kind, each needing different mathematics: exact (Hash(x)=h), empirical (P(X>x)), interpretive (Meaning(x,C)), normative (Authorized(a,p)) -- resolving the previous risk of treating every architectural property as probabilistically quantifiable.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Set/Logic + Probability/Statistics + Semantics + Graph Theory.
b_rows_sample.statement: KnowledgeOS is proposed to span four mathematical domains: Logic (handles invariants), Statistics (uncertainty and empirical evidence), Semantics (meaning and context), Graph theory (lineage and transformation history) -- a more defensible architecture than reducing everything to one equation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeItem, Transformation, EvidenceRecord, Decision, Policy, ProvenanceRecord. Each aggregate protects its own invariants.
b_rows_sample.statement: Candidate DDD aggregate boundaries (avoiding one enormous transactional aggregate): KnowledgeItem, Transformation, EvidenceRecord, Decision, Policy, ProvenanceRecord, each with its own invariant -- e.g. KnowledgeItem 'cannot change materially without a recorded transition'; Transformation 'cannot be considered governed without an applicable authority/policy decision'; EvidenceRecord 'cannot silently change after being used to support a claim' (a source change must produce a new evidence state); Decision = f(Evidence,Authority,Context,Policy), not authoritative merely by existing; Policy determines AllowedTransformations/RequiredEvidence/RequiredAuthority/RequiredValidation, giving Policy->GovernedTransformation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ObservationRecorded, EvidenceRegistered, ClaimProposed, KnowledgeAccepted, TransformationRequested, TransformationExecuted, ValidationCompleted, DecisionApproved, KnowledgeSuperseded.
b_rows_sample.statement: Nine candidate domain events forming the temporal history, supporting an event-sourced interpretation K_t = Fold(E_1,...,E_t), i.e. CurrentState = f(EventHistory) -- explicitly noted as an implementation choice, not a mandatory architecture requirement.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \mathcal K=(State,Context,Transformation,Evidence,Authority) with Lineage being generated by the sequence of transformations: L=History(T).
b_rows_sample.statement: The kernel is reduced from the original 6-tuple (K,C,T,A,E,L) to a 5-tuple (K,C,T,E,A) by recognizing Lineage L is not independent but generated by the transformation history: L = History(T) -- an important reduction toward the minimal kernel.

b_rows_sample.anchor: SI=f(K,C,T) ... BP=f(C,T) ... EI=f(K,E) ... GA=f(A,T) ... TL=f(T_{1:n}) ... DA=f(E,T,Policy). ... the seven principles may not be seven fundamental architectural primitives. They may be derived properties.
b_rows_sample.statement: Candidate dependency equations deriving the 6 (of the earlier 7-8) named architectural principles as functions of the minimal kernel: SemanticIntegrity=f(K,C,T), BoundaryPreservation=f(C,T), EpistemicIntegrity=f(K,E), GovernedAction=f(A,T), TemporalLineage=f(T_{1:n}), Assurance/DeterministicAssurance=f(E,T,Policy) -- proposing that these principles may be derived properties rather than independent primitives, precisely the compression the historical audit sought.

a_rows_sample.statement: Elaborates the earlier Zero/Lord/Sarathi/Transition division with explicit role definitions: Zero detects gaps/conflicts/boundaries; Lord expands the possibility space; Sarathi navigates/guides; Transition actually changes state. The earlier Sarathi formalization is given a full function signature: Sarathi(K_t, Z_t, L_t, I_t, Q_t, C_t) -> a_t, where a_t is the next epistemic action -- described as remarkably close to what is now called action selection/guidance, though the modern formal model deliberately avoids promoting the old lens vocabulary into architectural objects. Confirms the earlier KnowledgeOS-as-Epistemic-Sarathi formulation (rather than an answer engine) and its See != Guide != Decide principle, noting it later became compatible with the modern formal chain Evidence != Determination != Proposal != Decision != Authorization != Action.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Z(I_t)\rightarrow \{\text{Undefined Criterion, Unassessed Risk, Hidden Assumption}\} ... I_{t+1}=Revision(I_t,U_t). ... \boxed{\text{The Sārathi may challenge the Ideal State, but the Knower owns the revision.}}
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes the 'Before We Continue' principle with explicit notation: when current understanding is insufficient, the system can challenge the objective itself. Z(I_t) -> {Undefined Criterion, Unassessed Risk, Hidden Assumption} detects deficiencies in the Ideal State I_t; L(I_t) -> {Possible New Goal Dimensions} expands it; followed by I_{t+1} = Revision(I_t, U_t). The governing rule: the Sarathi may challenge the Ideal State, but the Knower owns the revision -- explicitly named as one of the strongest bridges between the old Step-series theory and the concurrent Gita Chapters 1-4 interpretation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Early conceptual model ↓ KnowledgeState / lenses / journey ↓ Sārathi + Zero + Lord separation ↓ "Before we continue" / objective revision ↓ formal Questions ↓ 25-series formalization ↓ Step 049 kernel reduction ↓ Step 050 adversarial audit ↓ falsification ↓ v0.2 canonical synthesis ↓ Final Architecture ↓ mathematical re-audit
a_rows_sample.statement: Sketches a twelve-stage historical evolution pipeline: early conceptual model -> KnowledgeState/lenses/journey -> Sarathi+Zero+Lord separation -> 'before we continue'/objective revision -> formal Questions -> the 25-series formalization -> Step 049 kernel reduction -> Step 050 adversarial audit -> falsification -> v0.2 canonical synthesis -> Final Architecture -> the current mathematical re-audit (GN-46, S1326). Characterizes v0.2 as a compression and purification of a much larger body of theory, explaining why current Edition-2 production is finding exactly the gaps it is finding. Recommends, rather than reconstructing artificial Step numbers beyond 156, building a four-way crosswalk: Step-era theory <-> v0.2 formal model <-> mathematical research <-> Gita Chapters 1-4, which would show which ideas were already discovered, formally retained, compressed, left open, rediscovered philosophically, and are now testable mathematically -- framed as a much stronger intellectual history of KnowledgeOS than simply claiming the Gita inspired the architecture. Poses an unresolved open research question: what mathematical object is actually produced by epistemic discernment -- a single action a_t in A, a three-valued classification D(K_t,G,Policy) -> {Permitted, Forbidden, Undetermined} over candidate actions, or a map D: A -> {epistemically justified classes}? Explicitly states this is not yet known.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero = What are we missing? ... Lord = What else could exist? ... Sārathi = What should the Knower investigate/do next?
b_rows_sample.statement: Establishes a three-way division of epistemic responsibility: Zero asks what is missing, Lord asks what else could exist (expanding the investigation space beyond currently known candidate dimensions), and Sarathi determines what the Knower should investigate or do next -- with the Knower retaining the roles of understand/decide/act.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS = Knowledge Model + Epistemic Operations ... Epistemic Operations: Zero Lens, Lord Lens, Krishna/Sarathi
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a preliminary two-part KnowledgeOS architecture: a Knowledge Model (Observation, Knowledge, Evidence, Dimension, Relationship, Ideal State) plus Epistemic Operations (Zero Lens, Lord Lens, Krishna/Sarathi), sitting beneath the Human Knower/Decision layer.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Sārathi = orchestrator of dimension discovery and investigation ... coordinates: Intent -> Candidate dimensions -> Observation -> Zero -> Lord -> Dimension refinement -> Next inquiry
b_rows_sample.statement: Sharpens Sarathi's role from generic 'answering questions' to a specific orchestration function coordinating intent, candidate dimensions, observation, Zero, Lord, dimension refinement and next inquiry, returning results to the Knower.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Sārathi(K,Z,L,Q) \rightarrow NextEpistemicAction ... ASK_KNOWER, OBSERVE, SEARCH, MEASURE, REQUEST_EVIDENCE, COMPARE, RECONCILE, EXPAND_DIMENSIONS, REVISE_QUESTION, STOP
b_rows_sample.statement: Generalizes Sarathi from guiding evidence-collection specifically to choosing among a named enumerable set of next epistemic actions (ASK_KNOWER, OBSERVE, SEARCH, MEASURE, REQUEST_EVIDENCE, COMPARE, RECONCILE, EXPAND_DIMENSIONS, REVISE_QUESTION, STOP), completing the full pipeline Knower->Intent->SemanticReconstruction->DimensionDiscovery->Proposition->Evidence->Assertion->EpistemicEvaluation->KnowledgeState->{Zero,Lord}->Sarathi->NextEpistemicAction.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Sarathi needs an additional parameter: Policy_t ... a_t = Sarathi(K_t,I_t,Z_t,L_t,Q_t,C_t,Policy_t)
b_rows_sample.statement: Adds an explicit Policy parameter to Sarathi's signature, since choosing between 'investigate first' and 'accept uncertainty' depends on purpose, risk, authority, cost, governance and evidence policy that cannot be inferred from the Knowledge/Ideal/Zero/Lord state alone.

b_rows_sample.anchor:
Instead of: Query -> Retrieve -> Answer
KnowledgeOS implements: Zero -> Gap -> Sarathi -> Retrieval -> Observation -> Evidence -> Knowledge -> Zero
This is a closed-loop epistemic investigation system, not a question-answering system.
b_rows_sample.statement: Contrasts RAG's open Query->Retrieve->Answer loop against a proposed closed-loop "epistemic retrieval loop" for KnowledgeOS: Zero detects a gap, Sarathi produces an investigation/retrieval plan, retrieval yields observations, observations become evidence, evidence updates the Knowledge State, and the updated state re-enters Zero -- framing KnowledgeOS as an investigation system rather than a question-answering system.

b_rows_sample.anchor:
class GitaKnowledgeOS:
    """Complete KnowledgeOS derived from Bhagavad-gītā Chapter 4."""
b_rows_sample.statement: An integrated GitaKnowledgeOS class composes all twelve verse-derived components (lineage, memory, intervention, reward, duty, attachment, dual_analyzer, wise_state, evidence_paths, benefit, learning, closure) alongside the existing Zero/Lord/Sarathi lenses, with an evolve(event) method implementing an eight-step pipeline: observe (Sanjaya) -> interpret (semantic) -> evaluate (Zero, detect_gaps) -> generate (Lord, generate_candidates) -> guide (Sarathi, recommend) -> act (Arjuna, conditional on closure.is_ready_to_act()) -> learn (apply learning.learn()) -> purify (apply learning.purify()). A semantic-extraction helper (_extract_semantics) pattern-matches on literal substring presence in observation content ('action', 'teacher'/'wisdom', 'offering'/'sacrifice') to route to different SemanticStructure types, falling back to a generic 'GeneralObservation' type otherwise.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS was explicitly described as an **"Epistemic Sārathi"** guiding the Knower through an evolving knowledge journey, rather than functioning as an answer oracle. ... $$\boxed{\text{See} \neq \text{Guide} \neq \text{Decide}}$$
b_rows_sample.statement: Recovered earlier (Step 155/156) material describes KnowledgeOS as an 'Epistemic Sarathi' guiding the Knower through an evolving knowledge journey rather than functioning as an answer oracle, with the role separation See != Guide != Decide, corresponding to observation/reconstruction, Sarathi guidance, and the human Knower's decision/action respectively. Question 17 in that earlier work already explicitly asked how Zero, Lord, and Sarathi interact with the transition system, with the distinction Zero != Lord != Sarathi != Transition and the composite claim Zero + Lord + Sarathi = Epistemic Guidance System.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the earlier work had already formulated the **"before we continue"** principle: if understanding is insufficient, the Sārathi can challenge the current objective, while the **Knower remains the owner of the revision**. ... I don't want to jump to that conclusion until I read the actual Step 155/156 texts.
b_rows_sample.statement: The recovered earlier work formulated a 'before we continue' principle: if understanding is insufficient, the Sarathi may challenge the current objective, but the Knower remains the owner of any revision -- explicitly noted as very close to the interpretation being extracted from Gita Chapters 1-4 concurrently. The earlier work also had a richer K_t: K_t = (A_t, R_t, E_t, H_t, Z_t, L_t), with assertions, relationships, evidence, history, Zero findings, and Lord candidates explicitly separated. Despite noting a potential historical convergence (earlier Step work: KnowledgeOS = Sarathi -> guide the epistemic journey -> expose Zero -> challenge insufficient objectives -> Knower decides; versus Gita 1-4 interpretation: crisis -> discrimination -> duty/action -> wisdom -> determine what should/should not be done), the author explicitly refuses to conclude convergence until the actual Step 155/156 texts are read, and commits to treating Step 155/156 as the authoritative historical baseline for that future comparison rather than reconstructing it from memory.

b_rows_sample.anchor: See ≠ Guide ≠ Decide ... This is much stronger than introducing Θ_A. Does the Knower/Sārathi distinction provide an ontological boundary for KnowledgeOS state? That is a legitimate architectural question.
b_rows_sample.statement: Argues that the Sanjaya(see)/Sarathi(guide)/human-Knower(decide) three-way distinction, already present in the KnowledgeOS architecture, is a stronger and more defensible Gita correspondence than the rejected Θ_A operator, and poses whether this Knower/Sarathi distinction can supply an ontological state boundary as a legitimate open architectural question.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The Bayesian formalism provides a complete mathematical foundation for KnowledgeOS's epistemic state, updating mechanism, confirmation theory, decision theory, and justification.
b_rows_sample.statement: The document's culminating 'complete formal system for KnowledgeOS': Sigma_t = {cr_t(P): P in L} as the epistemic state; Sigma_{t+1} = Sigma_t(.|E_t) (or Jeffrey Conditionalization for uncertain evidence) as the transition; confirmation as E confirms H iff Sigma_t(H|E) > Sigma_t(H); decision as a_t = argmax_A sum_i u(A&S_i)*Sigma_t(S_i|A) (EDT) or the CDT analogue; and the Three Lenses re-stated as Zero (regularity/confirmation-measures/Scott Axiom), Lord (Bayes's theorem/likelihood ratios), Sarathi (decision theory/Conditionalization). Final claim: 'These are now formally available to KnowledgeOS' -- asserted without independent derivation or proof of fit to the prior KnowledgeOS kernel formalizations.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Lord(K_t,Z_t,G,H_t) -> Proposal. It does not own the epistemic frame. ... S_t(K_t,Z_t,G,H_t,Proposal) -> Decision. Proposal != Decision.
b_rows_sample.statement: Gives refined typed signatures for Lord (Lord(K_t,Z_t,G,H_t) -> Proposal, explicitly not owning the epistemic frame) and Sarathi (S_t(K_t,Z_t,G,H_t,Proposal) -> Decision), re-affirming Proposal != Decision as an important invariant, and situates both within a full epistemic control loop Observation -> Evidence -> Extraction -> Determination -> K_t -> {IdealState, Zero} -> Gap Delta_t -> Lord -> Proposal -> Sarathi -> Decision -> authorization -> Action -> new Observation -> K_{t+1}.

b_rows_sample.anchor: d* = argmax_d E[Delta G_t | investigate d]. ... a_t* = argmax_a E[epistemic improvement|a] / cost(a)
b_rows_sample.statement: Gives Lord a concrete dimension-discovery objective -- choose the new dimension d expected to most reduce the epistemic-gap vector, d*=argmax_d E[Delta-G_t | investigate d] -- and Sarathi a concrete cost-normalized action-selection objective a_t*=argmax_a E[epistemic improvement|a]/cost(a), framed as deriving the architecture from the mathematics rather than the reverse.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 'Yoni Lens' -> Epistemic Generation Context (G_gen): An outer-kernel proposal engine that formulates candidate node assertions ASSERT(p) and link transitions LINK(p1,p2) ... 'Zero Lens' -> Epistemic Evaluation & Isolation Context (E_eval): The non-mutating analysis layer that runs EVal(K,p,Gamma), identifies partial/theory-blocked states, and triggers ISOLATE(p) when structural contradictions are detected ... b_rows_sample.statement: Maps the three metaphoric 'Lenses' of the reviewed proposal onto verified Kernel v1.3 interfaces: Yoni Lens becomes an Epistemic Generation Context that proposes ASSERT/LINK candidate operations; Zero Lens becomes an Epistemic Evaluation & Isolation Context running EVal and triggering ISOLATE on detected structural contradiction; Sarathi Lens becomes the already-specified Determination Bridge Det. The three-role shape (generative proposal / boundary evaluation / decision guidance) closely parallels the corpus's earlier Zero/Lord/Sarathi guidance cycle, with the generative role renamed from 'Lord' to 'Yoni'.

a_rows_sample.statement: Rejects a naive first formulation a*=argmax_a VOI(a) as insufficient because VOI captures only information/decision value and ignores authorization, safety, cost, urgency, dependencies, and reversibility.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A_{feasible}=\{a\in A\mid Feasible(a,K,C)\} ... a^*=Select(A_{feasible},Objective)
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes the two-stage algorithm: first compute A_feasible = {a in A | Feasible(a,K,C)}, then a* = Select(A_feasible, Objective); Lord's two responsibilities are therefore (1) remove impossible/unauthorized actions, (2) choose among the remaining — 'Feasibility -> Optimization.'

a_rows_sample.statement: Depicts the action dependency graph Lord can traverse to reach the root-gap-resolving action.

a_rows_sample.anchor: EU(q)=\sum_e P(e\mid q,K)\max_a EU(a\mid K,e) ... VOI(q)=EU(q)-EU(a^*) ... optional specialized engine, not part of the epistemic kernel
a_rows_sample.statement: Gives the classical statistical/decision-theoretic version: EU(q)=sum_e P(e|q,K) max_a EU(a|K,e); VOI(q)=EU(q)-EU(a*); explicitly classified as 'an optional specialized engine, not part of the epistemic kernel.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: D15. step-025g (183746) -- Formal Lord Algebra ... section6 action utility vector A=(Purpose,ExpectedGain,Cost,Risk,Urgency,Reversibility,Authorization,Dependencies,Deadline) ... section19 Prefer(a1,a2|K,G,C) rather than Score(a) ... section24 the default Lord policy ... section54 commissions 025H (Sarathi)
b_rows_sample.statement: Step-025g (file 183746) formalizes Lord(K_t,Z_t,G,C) -> a_t, splitting Action into EpistemicAction (q: K_t -> K_{t+1}) and OperationalAction (a: W_t -> W_{t+1}) under the rule 'Lord selects; Governance authorizes; Executor executes'; rejects a^*=argmax VOI(a) as insufficient and instead defines a nine-dimension action utility vector A=(Purpose,ExpectedGain,Cost,Risk,Urgency,Reversibility,Authorization,Dependencies,Deadline), explicitly refusing a collapsed scalar Score(A) that 'would hide semantics'; uses a two-stage feasibility-then-optimization algorithm and root-gap analysis (graph reasoning, not LLM intuition); offers an optional statistical expected-utility engine but favors a qualitative preference relation Prefer(a1,a2|K,G,C) (deliberately arg-prefer, not arg-max-Score, 'we have not yet established that these dimensions can legitimately be collapsed'); states Capability != Authority; states the default Lord policy verbatim ('prefer the least risky authorized action that maximally reduces decision-critical Zero, subject to cost, dependencies and deadlines'); defines a termination algebra {Completed,Blocked,Escalated,Abandoned,Expired} with DoNothing in ActionSpace and 'no action is preferable to an unjustified action'; runs five experiments and six falsification passes, including the finding that high information value cannot override governance and that an LLM recommendation cannot override Zero/Contract; and commissions Sarathi (step-025H) as the next research item, delivered the following day outside this batch.

Only ONE pair reaches Level 3: Ω-A × Ω-2. And it reaches it on a byte-identical signature with identical glosses — while citing the wrong source.
a_rows_sample.statement: Runs a three-level (lexical/mathematical/semantic) identity test across all Omega-sense pairs: finds Omega-A and Omega-2 (from 031) reach full Level-3 SAME-OBJECT status with a byte-identical W->O signature and identical W/O glosses, but Omega-A mis-attributes its provenance to D285-6 rather than 031; Omega-B and Omega-4/7 are DISTINCT-EXPLICIT since the corpus explicitly rejects Omega=K; Omega-B and Omega-A are IDENTITY UNWITNESSED (neither document mentions the other, despite both being definitionally developed); Omega-C and Omega-5 (the s236 operation-set reading) are RELATED with no citation; Omega-C and O_core (s277) are RELATED-IDENTITY-UNWITNESSED; Omega-D's internal type error makes it UNDECIDABLE. Notes the two most-developed Omega senses in this interval (the horizon document and the Sanjaya document) never mention each other at all.

a_rows_sample.anchor: §7 · C-06 — a local ruling against COMBINING, not a global verdict on Ω ... C-06 adjudicates that two HOMONYMS must not be combined. It does NOT rule that Ω is contradictory. ... the corpus independently reaches the same separation five days later ... CORROBORATIVE, and by §9 this counts as two lineages, not two documents.
a_rows_sample.statement: Re-examines the corpus's own C-06 'TRUE CONTRADICTION' ruling (Omega=Knowledge Space vs Omega:W->O) verbatim, identifying it addresses specifically Omega-7 vs Omega-2, contradicting the 031 non-identifiability result, is a mathematical+semantic (set vs function) type incompatibility, concerns objects G-22 already classed DISTINCT, and crucially is BOUNDED/conditional ('combining them WOULD make...') rather than a global verdict. Concludes C-06 rules only that two homonyms must not be COMBINED, not that Omega itself is contradictory. Notes the corpus independently reaches the identical separation five days later via Omega-B's explicit rejection of Omega=K, in a different lane, with no citation between the two -- classified as two independent (CORROBORATIVE) lineages rather than a single duplicated finding.

a_rows_sample.anchor: §12 · Continuity with apparatus loss — the Ω instance, and it is sharper than 026's ... A gap was opened for an object the corpus had DEFINED THREE DAYS EARLIER — and then closed by 'recovering' it. ... apparatus never left the corpus — only the working set — and its re-discovery was recorded as a gap closure.
a_rows_sample.statement: Traces a precise sequence: 031 defines Omega:W->O boxed (08-28 10:22) -> a 155-file silence -> Omega returns (08-29) -> step_251 cites it unattributed (08-30) -> a NEW GAP is explicitly opened ('Gap 1: (W,Omega) referent layer', 08-31 19:03) -> the same gap is closed hours later by 'recovering' the Sanjaya layer (08-31 19:52, G3->G5) -> a claim that 'the earlier claim that the verification lane lacked an entire observation/referent layer is no longer valid' (08-31 19:40) -> Omega-A's document frames this as resolving 'a structural omission discovered in D285-6' (08-31 20:11). Concludes a gap was opened for an object the corpus had already defined three days earlier, then closed by 'recovering' it -- the corpus does not record this as a loss, it records it as a discovery. Contrasts this with G-12's 026 mechanism ('continuity declared, apparatus not carried'): here, the apparatus never left the corpus at all, only the ACTIVE WORKING SET did, and its re-discovery was mislabeled a gap closure -- two distinct mechanisms in one family, recorded as evidence not generalized into a law.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The corpus draws the right distinction itself ... 'Observation' being recovered closes the discovery gap, but the executable semantics of Ω and Qualify are not thereby solved. Discovery gap ≠ semantic gap — stated by the corpus, and correct.
a_rows_sample.statement: Notes approvingly that the corpus itself already draws the correct distinction: recovering Omega's observation-layer definition closes only a DISCOVERY gap, not the underlying SEMANTIC gap (executable semantics of Omega and Qualify remain unsolved) -- endorsed here as a stated-and-correct corpus self-observation, not a finding original to this investigation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: §8 · Distributed completeness ... Ω-A COMPLETE THROUGH MULTIPLE SOURCES ... Ω-B GENUINE CORPUS GAP (bounded: Ω-B only) ... Ω-C IDENTITY UNRESOLVED ... Ω-D UNDECIDABLE
a_rows_sample.statement: Tests distributed completeness per sense: Omega-A is COMPLETE THROUGH MULTIPLE SOURCES (031 supplies the non-identifiability result Omega-A itself omits); Omega-B is a GENUINE CORPUS GAP, explicitly bounded to Omega-B only -- searched across all 55 Omega files plus the whole non-firewalled corpus, no type/domain/codomain is ever given for the 'horizon' concept; Omega-C is IDENTITY UNRESOLVED (operations named but the set never enumerated; s277's O_core enumerates a candidate set with unwitnessed identity); Omega-D is UNDECIDABLE due to its internal type inconsistency.

a_rows_sample.anchor: §10 · Mathematical audit (Ω-A PROVEN function W→O, Ω-B UNKNOWN never typed, Ω-C PROVEN as a set/UNKNOWN membership, Ω-D contradictory within one file) ... No TYPE-CONSTRAINED value was promoted to PROVEN. §11 · DDD audit ... Four bounded-context candidates, one glyph, zero context mappings.
a_rows_sample.statement: Mathematical audit: Omega-A is PROVEN as function W->O; Omega-B is UNKNOWN, never typed at all; Omega-C is PROVEN as a finite set but its membership is UNKNOWN; Omega-D is contradictory within one file (measure space and element set simultaneously). Notes no type-constrained value in this audit was ever promoted to PROVEN status. DDD audit assigns each Omega sense to a distinct bounded context (Omega-A observation/referent layer -- map reality to observation; Omega-B epistemic framing/Gita lens -- situate a finite state against a horizon, explicitly Omega!=K and Omega!=God per the corpus; Omega-C kernel -- delimit permitted operations; Omega-D Gita-derived mathematics -- integration domain/state set), concluding four bounded-context candidates share one glyph with zero context mappings between them.

a_rows_sample.anchor: §16 · Terminal conditions (8 corpus-wide Ω objects, 4 live in 269–291; classification E overall — OBJECT IDENTITY UNRESOLVED, per-sense: Ω-A B, Ω-B D (genuine gap, bounded), Ω-C E, Ω-D E)
a_rows_sample.statement: Answers eight terminal questions: 8 Omega objects exist corpus-wide (Omega-1..Omega-8 combining G-22 and G-12 findings), 4 live in 269-291 (A,B,C,D); genuine birth points identified (Omega-A actually born at 031, 08-28, not 08-31 as its own document implies; Omega-B 09-01 01:17; Omega-C 09-01 00:53; Omega-D 08-28 23:52); the windows overlap 44 hours; identity results are 1 SAME OBJECT (A x Omega-2), 1 DISTINCT-EXPLICIT (B x Omega-4/7), 2 RELATED (C), rest UNWITNESSED; C-06 adjudicates specifically Omega-7 x Omega-2 and is LOCAL not global; 269-291 completes 031's Omega-2 partially (restoring the signature and glosses but omitting the non-identifiability result and mis-attributing the source); exactly one genuine bounded semantic gap exists (Omega-B is never typed). Final classification: Omega as a whole = class E (OBJECT IDENTITY UNRESOLVED, four live senses, one glyph, one Level-3 identity established, zero context mappings); per-sense Omega-A=B (complete through multiple sources), Omega-B=D (genuine gap, bounded), Omega-C=E, Omega-D=E. Explicitly notes class A was not forced onto any sense.

a_rows_sample.anchor: §14 · Negative history ... Not found: any type/domain/codomain for Ω-B; any document identifying Ω-A with Ω-B; any citation from Ω-A to 031; any context mapping between the four senses. ⇒ GENUINE CORPUS GAP for Ω-B's type only; everything else IDENTITY UNWITNESSED.
a_rows_sample.statement: Confirms a negative-history search across all 168 step-269-291 files (both spellings) plus the whole non-firewalled corpus for Omega-B's type finds nothing: no type/domain/codomain for Omega-B, no document identifying Omega-A with Omega-B, no citation from Omega-A back to 031, and no context mapping between the four live senses. Classifies exactly one item as GENUINE CORPUS GAP (Omega-B's type) and everything else as IDENTITY UNWITNESSED rather than gap. Confirms Det_r and any firewalled Omega history remain FIREWALL-LIMITED; firewall honoured, nothing canonicalized, no Omega sense selected or merged.

a_rows_sample.anchor: §14 · ⛔ G-26 REFUTED — Ω-B is untyped by design ... Ω-B's actual history ... begins 2026-08-26 14:35 ... six days earlier, 33 files ... Lord Lens (Ω): Represents the total, unbounded, and potentially infinite knowledge space. ... It is not a part of the system but a philosophical anchor ... Ω_B is untyped BECAUSE ITS OWN DEFINITION EXCLUDES IT FROM THE SYSTEM.
a_rows_sample.statement: Refutes the investigation's own previously-opened G-26 gap claim ('Omega-B has no type anywhere in the non-firewalled corpus') by applying its own required birth-point method to Omega-B: finds Omega-B's real history begins six days earlier than claimed (2026-08-26 14:35, 33 files, not 2026-09-01), in a 'Lord Lens (Omega)' document that explicitly states Omega-B represents 'the total, unbounded, and potentially infinite knowledge space... the ultimate epistemic horizon... It is not a part of the system but a philosophical anchor for the system's purpose... the system's epistemic conscience.' Concludes Omega-B is untyped BECAUSE its own definition explicitly excludes it from the system -- not a corpus gap but a declared scope exclusion. Notes the same document places Omega-B as the source of the system's top-level pipeline equation (KnowledgeOS: Omega -Zero Lens-> S_t -Krishna Lens-> A_t -> ... -> Knower's Decision), so it is not inert despite being excluded. Re-scopes G-26 (not closed as a gap) to a narrower modelling question: is a philosophical anchor appearing as the domain of the system's top-level equation still meaningfully 'outside the system'? Notes this is the third time this method has overturned one of the investigation's own gap claims (after EvalReq's codomain and V_Sat's consumers), establishing the self-critical pattern as measured rather than merely suspected: 'I open gaps from bounded searches.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: §1–4 · The 025→026 boundary, object by object — and my G-12 headline qualified ... The concepts did not stop. They de-formalised. ... sufficiency 73% ... satisfaction 45% ... contract 40% ... The NOTATION was lost. The CONCEPTS ran on through 45–73% of the interval.
a_rows_sample.statement: Qualifies the prior G-12 finding that the 025 apparatus 'vanishes' at step 026: while all formal 025 SYMBOLS score exactly 0 across 265 files (confirmed true), a census of the underlying 025-era CONCEPTS in prose form finds sufficiency at 73% (193/265 files), satisfaction at 45% (120/265), contract at 40% (107/265), gap at 20%, acceptance criterion at 2%, while the specific phrase 'requirement evaluation' scores 0. Concludes the NOTATION was lost but the CONCEPTS ran on informally through 45-73% of the interval -- the earlier headline ('the apparatus vanishes') is true only of formal notation, not of underlying concepts.

a_rows_sample.anchor: And precisely which form survived ... Of 241 satisf* occurrences sampled: 83 in technical context, 158 prose. ... What survived is satisfaction as a PREDICATE. What was lost is satisfaction as a TYPED FUNCTION WITH A RESULT SPACE.
a_rows_sample.statement: Samples 241 'satisf*' occurrences (83 technical, 158 prose) and verifies at ten specific steps (s070,079,081,086,091,092,095,097,098,101) that the surviving technical usage is uniformly an unformalised predicate ('the rule is satisfied', 'invariants remain satisfied') rather than the 025-series typed function Satisfied(K,r,EC) with three typed arguments and a result space S(9->10->11). Concludes precisely what survived was satisfaction AS A PREDICATE; what was lost was satisfaction as a TYPED FUNCTION WITH A RESULT SPACE.

a_rows_sample.anchor: An interpretation, marked as such ... consistent with — and would explain — the four divergent Sat codomains found in G-25 ... nothing carried a result space through the interval, so each later lane supplied its own. ⛔ Recorded as [PROPOSED], not as a cause.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes, explicitly marked as an unproven interpretation (not a corpus-stated cause), that the loss of a shared result space during the interval would explain why G-25 later found four mutually non-citing Sat codomains (S 9-11, V_Sat 3, S_sat 4, S_sat variant): each later lane, lacking an inherited result space, supplied its own. Notes this hypothesis is recorded as [PROPOSED] rather than established, citing a cautionary precedent -- a previously withdrawn batch-003 claim ('the semantics-bearing argument always disappears') that failed for exactly the same overreach.

a_rows_sample.anchor: §6 · Distributed completeness — the corrected classification ... EvalReq is the only 025-era object whose concept as well as its notation leaves the interval. That singles it out, and it is the one object G-25 found still untyped at 09-06.
a_rows_sample.statement: Provides a corrected four-row classification: '025 apparatus vanishes at 026' is corrected from PARTIALLY-EVIDENCED to DE-FORMALISED (symbols 0, concepts 45-73%); 'Sat is absent from 026-268' stands for the FUNCTION but is FALSE for the underlying CONCEPT (0 vs 120 files); 'EvalReq is absent' stands fully, both notation and concept (even the phrase 'requirement evaluation' scores 0/265); 'Omega-B has no type' is REFUTED (excluded by design, per S14). Concludes EvalReq is uniquely the only 025-era object whose CONCEPT, not merely its notation, actually leaves the interval -- and it is the same object G-25 separately found still untyped as late as 09-06.

a_rows_sample.anchor: §8, §12 · Identity and DDD — EC is the interval's worst case ... Three ECs, three arities, three bounded contexts, zero cross-references ... Verdict: HOMONYM ×3, IDENTITY UNWITNESSED between every pair.
a_rows_sample.statement: Identifies EC as a triple homonym with zero cross-references between any pair: EC=EpistemicClaim (s032, 11-tuple, 'the atomic unit of KnowledgeOS'); EC=engineering change (s117, 8-tuple, 'a test object' in a traceability experiment); EC=EpistemicContract (025-series, (R_G,Gamma_G) shape, 0 occurrences in steps 026-154). Classifies this as HOMONYM x3 with IDENTITY UNWITNESSED between every pair, noting it is the same shape of finding as Determination (governance vs mathematical vs Det_r) and Gamma (four senses), already recorded elsewhere in this programme.

a_rows_sample.anchor: §7 · Mathematical typing across the interval (PROVEN: Ω-2, K_v0, K_v1, EC-claim, Γ_A, EC-engchange; UNKNOWN: Zero never defined, Δ_t only α_t defined, Ω_t unresolved, Update 10 signatures) ... No promotion of TYPE-CONSTRAINED or INFERRED to PROVEN.
a_rows_sample.statement: Audits mathematical typing status across the interval: PROVEN objects include Omega-2 (W->O), K_v0 (9-tuple, s028), K_v1 (7-tuple, s031), EC-claim (11-tuple, s032), Gamma_A (4-tuple, s053), EC-engchange (8-tuple, s117); UNKNOWN status objects include Zero (never defined anywhere in 265 files), Delta_t (one occurrence, whose 'where' clause defines only a sub-component alpha_t, not Delta_t itself), Omega_t as an argument of delta_K (signature declared unresolved by its own cited sources), and Update (10 unrelated signatures). Notes no TYPE-CONSTRAINED or INFERRED-status object was promoted to PROVEN in this pass.

a_rows_sample.anchor: §11 · Senior-statistician audit ('satisfaction continues' 120 files/many independent lineages; '025 symbols absent' 0 hits × 265 files/1 measurement; Ω-B 'philosophical anchor' 33 files/1 lineage)
a_rows_sample.statement: Applies the programme's senior-statistician discipline (distinguishing occurrence counts from independent evidential lineages) to its own three headline claims: 'satisfaction continues' (120 files) is genuinely MANY independent lineages spread across s070-s101+ and multiple sub-lanes; '025 symbols are absent' (0 hits x 265 files) is only ONE measurement, not 265 confirmations; Omega-B's 'philosophical anchor' framing (33 files) is only ONE lineage, a single continuous Gita/Lord-Lens thread from 08-26 onward.

a_rows_sample.anchor: §15 · Classification of what this pass touched (Ω-B upgraded B; satisfaction-concept B / satisfaction-function C; EvalReq D genuine corpus gap for the interval, exhausted search; EC E; Zero/Δ_t E)
a_rows_sample.statement: Issues final classifications for this pass: Omega-B is upgraded from D to class B (COMPLETE THROUGH MULTIPLE SOURCES -- defined semantically at birth, its absent type being a declared exclusion, not a gap); the satisfaction CONCEPT is class B (continues as a predicate across the interval) while the satisfaction FUNCTION remains class C (competing definitions, per G-25); EvalReq is class D (GENUINE CORPUS GAP for the interval specifically, on an now-exhausted search -- both notation and concept score 0 in all 265 files); EC is class E (OBJECT IDENTITY UNRESOLVED, three homonyms); Zero and Delta_t are class E (used throughout but never defined within the interval).

a_rows_sample.anchor: §10 · Negative-history discipline ... Coverage qualifier preserved: ≈1.5% of the readable corpus is read semantically. No corpus-wide negative claim is made from this slice — the EvalReq finding is scoped to the interval, and Ω-B's is scoped to its own 33-file history.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the negative-history search scope precisely (265 files of 026-268 plus the whole non-firewalled corpus for Omega-B's type across its 33-file history and for the 025 concepts) and preserves an explicit coverage qualifier: only approximately 1.5% (32 of 2,099 files) of the readable corpus has been read semantically by this whole gap-discovery programme so far. Explicitly refuses to generalize any finding beyond its search scope -- the EvalReq absence is scoped to this interval only, and Omega-B's exclusion-by-design finding is scoped to its own 33-file history only. Confirms firewall honoured, nothing canonicalized, no definition selected or merged.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A search defect found first, and it changes the count ... A glyph-only search returns 1 file of 11 and 2 occurrences of 28 — a 93% miss.
b_rows_sample.statement: Finds the corpus writes the symbol Omega two ways (Unicode glyph Omega and LaTeX \Omega): across steps 231-267 there are 28 total occurrences in 11 of 40 files, but a glyph-only search finds only 2 occurrences in 1 file -- a 93% miss rate -- establishing that any symbol sweep for this corpus must cover both notations.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Ω Sense Inventory — FIVE senses ... (Ω-1 ontology, Ω-2 observation, Ω-3 transition arg, Ω-4 state measure space, Ω-5 generic placeholder)
b_rows_sample.statement: Reconstructs five distinct in-window Omega senses with birth documents and identity status: Omega-1 'ontology' (Omega=domain ontology/rules, born 025k L53 2026-08-28 09:39, status CONTINUOUS within its family then RE-FOUNDED AWAY at 031); Omega-2 'observation' (Omega:W->O, defined 031 SS31.18 2026-08-28 10:22 as the observation mechanism, status IDENTITY-UNWITNESSED though byte-identical in type to 031); Omega-3 'transition arg' (untyped 4th argument of delta_K(K_t,o_t,rho_t,Omega_t), born step-016 L1993 2026-08-27 16:00, the OLDEST readable Omega, IDENTITY-UNWITNESSED, its own sources say the signature is unresolved); Omega-4 'state measure space' (Omega=K, the sample space IS the knowledge-state space, born 238 L16 during the R1 measure-theory phase, EXPLICITLY_REDEFINED then abandoned as a 'temptation'); Omega-5 'generic placeholder' (borrowed textbook notation for algebra/measurement/probability-space conventions, never a KnowledgeOS object, classified HOMONYM).

b_rows_sample.anchor: ⛔ Correction to my own prior finding ... Net: 6 → 5 senses, with one previously invisible collision inside a single document.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the investigation's own prior claim (09-EVIDENCE-LOG.md SS5) that Omega has six mutually incompatible meanings: that count over-counted Omega-4 across three retrospective-citation sites as three separate senses, under-attributed Omega:W->O's definitional source (031 SS31.18, two days before the 251 citation), and missed both Omega-1 (the 025-series ontology sense, co-occurring 300 lines from Omega:W->O in the same document step_251) and Omega-5 (236's explicit 'a set of operations' gloss). Net correction: 6 senses collapses to 5, revealing a previously invisible collision (Omega-1 and Omega-2 coexisting unremarked within a single document, step_251).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Ω_a / Ω_b / Ω_c — an explicit split record whose terms are never defined [later WITHDRAWN, see §12.1] ... The role survived as an invariant; whether the SYMBOL continued to denote it is a separate question the corpus does not answer.
b_rows_sample.statement: Records step_238's assertion that Omega diverged into three roles (Omega_a->IdealState/contract, Omega_b->dropped, Omega_c->complement principle => invariant I-7: X_t != Observed(X_t)) with no document (in the initially searched forms) defining the three terms individually; notes the ROLE carried by Omega_c demonstrably survives as invariant I-7 with the same semantics as Omega:W->O, but the corpus never states that the SYMBOL Omega_c became Omega:W->O -- recorded as IDENTITY-UNWITNESSED, not continuity. (This claim about Omega_a/b/c being undefined is itself later withdrawn in section 12.1 of the same file upon a wider evidence sweep.)

b_rows_sample.anchor: 4. Ω : W → O — located, typed, and its inheritance tested ... retained / weakened / altered / abandoned? RETAINED, unchanged, at the one site that carries it.
b_rows_sample.statement: Traces Omega:W->O to its definitional source (031 SS31.18 L598, boxed, 2026-08-28 10:22:51, with W_t='the relevant real-world state' and O_t=Obs(W_t) the partial observation) and tests inheritance: only step_251 (18:36, two days later) carries the byte-identical W->O signature, and it does so via an unattributed citation to 'the corpus' with no step number or explicit equivalence claim -- every other in-window Omega has a different or absent type. Status: RETAINED unchanged at the one site that carries it.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 5. Four histories, kept separate (Conceptual / Mathematical / Operational / Governance) ... A later mathematical redefinition has not overwritten an earlier conceptual record here — because there was never a redefinition. There were independent definitions that never met.
b_rows_sample.statement: Separates four independent histories for Omega: Conceptual (four unrelated referents -- derivation rule-set, world-to-observation mechanism, an unnamed fourth transition argument, and the space of possible knowledge states -- with no conceptual thread connecting them); Mathematical (one function W->O, one rule set, one measure-space carrier, one untyped argument, one borrowed placeholder -- only Omega-2 has a definitionally stated signature); Operational (Omega-1 consumed by Update/Derive, Omega-3 by delta_K, Omega-2 never consumed by any operation in the window, Omega-4 demoted from foundation to regime to 'temptation', Omega-5 never operational); Governance/history (R1, Omega-4's home, is classified a 'failed direction' with ALT-01 recorded -- but this claim of 'no governance act on Omega itself' is later withdrawn in section 12.2). Concludes there was never a redefinition overwriting an earlier record -- these were independent definitions that never met.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 6. Re-foundings — one explicit alignment, and it is the whole finding ... The symbol Ω crossed re-founding #1 and was re-used for a different object. Silently.
b_rows_sample.statement: Checks Omega's alignment against five known corpus re-foundings, finding only one decisive alignment: re-founding #1 (031, 'drops the 025 apparatus') explicitly drops the Omega-1=domain-ontology apparatus and, in the same document 43 minutes later, defines Omega:W->O as the observation mechanism, mentioning '025', 'domain ontology' or Update(K,E,Omega,EC) zero times. Re-foundings #2/#3/#5 show no Omega evidence; re-founding #4 (262, K=(A,R)) shows no alignment since Omega had already gone dark 51 minutes earlier; a shared classification with tau:SxC->S (Step 204) as sibling 'family' rows is explicitly recorded as classification only, not shared identity. Concludes the symbol Omega crossed re-founding #1 and was silently re-used for a different object.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 7. G-19 not used ... no Ω sense was preferred because it makes the K model work.
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly records that no primary source connects the G-19 falsification result to any Omega sense, and no Omega sense was adjudicated or preferred on the grounds that it makes the K model work -- an independence discipline note.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 8. Identity matrix — all ten pairs ... Not one pair of the ten is supported as the same object by any corpus evidence.
b_rows_sample.statement: Builds a complete ten-pair identity matrix over the five senses: Omega-1xOmega-2 HOMONYM (explicit, 43 minutes apart, type-incompatible, coexisting unremarked 300 lines apart in step_251); Omega-2xOmega-3 DISTINCT by explicit differentiation (step-016 separately names Obs(X_t,S_t) and a different fourth argument Omega_t in the same boxed formula); Omega-1xOmega-4, Omega-1xOmega-5, Omega-2xOmega-4, Omega-2xOmega-5 DISTINCT by type; Omega-1xOmega-3, Omega-3xOmega-4, Omega-3xOmega-5 UNDECIDABLE (Omega-3 untyped, sources say so); Omega-4xOmega-5 POSSIBLE SAME OBJECT-identity-unwitnessed (both measure-theoretic sample-space notation, but Omega-4 commits to Omega=K while Omega-5 is a placeholder). Tally: 1 HOMONYM, 1 DISTINCT-by-differentiation, 4 DISTINCT-by-type, 3 UNDECIDABLE, 1 POSSIBLE-SAME-UNWITNESSED, 0 SAME OBJECT -- not one of the ten pairs is supported as the same object by any corpus evidence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 9. Mandatory adversarial check — both directions ... The corpus had the instrument and did not turn it on itself.
b_rows_sample.statement: Runs a two-directional adversarial evidence check: (A) searching for evidence that senses ARE one continuous object -- no identifying statement, rename/supersession/retirement record, or type bridge found, so results are recorded IDENTITY-UNWITNESSED rather than assumed distinct; (B) searching for evidence senses ARE distinct -- finds two incompatible explicit definitions (025k vs 031, 43 minutes apart, neither citing the other), one document (step-016) naming the observation function Obs while using Omega for a different argument, and step_238's own explicit 'Same word != Same concept' DDD-lesson collision-marking rule (applied there to Zero and Lord). The self-referential finding: step_238 states this exact discipline as a lesson, applies it to Zero and Lord, and in the same document uses Omega in three different senses without applying the lesson to Omega itself -- the corpus had the instrument and did not turn it on itself.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 10. Findings G22-1 through G22-8
b_rows_sample.statement: Issues eight findings: G22-1 (CRITICAL) Omega-1xOmega-2 is a HOMONYM on explicit definitional evidence, born 43 minutes apart across re-founding #1, neither citing the other; G22-2 (CRITICAL) step_251 carries both senses simultaneously 300 lines apart and never notices, the same document G-03's Omega/EC sub-family classification rests on; G22-3 (HIGH, corrective) five senses not six, correcting an over-split of Omega-4 and a missed Omega-1/Omega-5; G22-4 (CRITICAL, method) a glyph-only search misses 93% of Omega occurrences in this window; G22-5 (HIGH) Omega-3 is the oldest readable Omega (step-016, 2026-08-27) and untyped at birth with a second undefined argument rho_t alongside it; G22-6 (UNRESOLVED, HIGH) the Omega_a/b/c split is asserted with three named roles and zero types; G22-7 (UNRESOLVED, MEDIUM) no governance act touches Omega -- rename/supersession/retirement/collision record absent; G22-8 (MEDIUM) step_238 states 'Same word != Same concept' as a DDD lesson, applies it to Zero and Lord, yet itself uses Omega in three senses in the same document.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 11. Scope discipline ... Ω-4's own sources call it a 'failed direction' and a 'temptation' — that is their classification, recorded, not adopted. ... Firewall: brainstorming/three_model_convergence/ was not opened
b_rows_sample.statement: Scopes the investigation: no sense is preferred, merged, repaired or retired; Omega-4's own sources' self-classification as a 'failed direction'/'temptation' is recorded, not adopted as the investigation's own judgment; three documents outside the 231-267 window were opened solely to type a symbol used inside it, importing no other content. Discloses the standing firewall: brainstorming/three_model_convergence/ was not opened, read, grepped or cited.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 12.1 ⛔ Ω_a / Ω_b / Ω_c ARE defined — two days before 238 cites them ... 238 reports as settled what its source recorded as unresolved, with no derivation shown.
b_rows_sample.statement: Retracts the earlier §3 claim: a wider evidence sweep (3,108 files, 493 containing Omega) finds Omega_a/Omega_b/Omega_c ARE defined, two days before step_238 cites them, in combine-prompt-4 (2026-08-28 15:01:40): Omega-a=ideal reference->Ideal State->Epistemic Contract, Omega-b=unboundedness->dropped, Omega-c=whole-space observation->unresolved. The miss was a notation-form defect (searched subscript \Omega_a rather than the corpus's dominant hyphenated Omega-a form), yielding the methodological correction that symbol sweeps must cover both subscript and hyphen forms. Also finds step_238 changed Omega-c's fate from 'unresolved' (source) to 'complement principle -> invariant I-7' with no derivation shown, and that two downstream records disagree on where Omega-c went (DISPLACED-no-host per combine-prompt-4/lord-omega-analysis vs TRANSFORMED-into-its-complement per 238/phase-2d-closure), recorded as unreconciled.

a_rows_sample.anchor:
class GitaKnowledgeOS:
    """Complete KnowledgeOS derived from Bhagavad-gītā Chapter 4."""
a_rows_sample.statement: An integrated GitaKnowledgeOS class composes all twelve verse-derived components (lineage, memory, intervention, reward, duty, attachment, dual_analyzer, wise_state, evidence_paths, benefit, learning, closure) alongside the existing Zero/Lord/Sarathi lenses, with an evolve(event) method implementing an eight-step pipeline: observe (Sanjaya) -> interpret (semantic) -> evaluate (Zero, detect_gaps) -> generate (Lord, generate_candidates) -> guide (Sarathi, recommend) -> act (Arjuna, conditional on closure.is_ready_to_act()) -> learn (apply learning.learn()) -> purify (apply learning.purify()). A semantic-extraction helper (_extract_semantics) pattern-matches on literal substring presence in observation content ('action', 'teacher'/'wisdom', 'offering'/'sacrifice') to route to different SemanticStructure types, falling back to a generic 'GeneralObservation' type otherwise.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Chapter 4 can give us additional architectural insight, but we should derive it as a set of architectural principles and testable hypotheses—not copy theological statements into the architecture.
a_rows_sample.statement: The central methodological rule for using Chapter 4 (and by extension any external/theological source) as KnowledgeOS research input: derive architectural principles and testable hypotheses from the source, never copy theological statements directly into the architecture. Nine principles are derived under this discipline: (1) knowledge has lineage -- K_t should conceptually be (content, provenance, status, history), not a bare object, though this equation is explicitly withheld from v0.2 pending testing; (2) loss of knowledge is not the same as invalid knowledge (NOT KNOWN NOW != NEVER KNOWN; CURRENTLY UNAVAILABLE != FALSE), supporting layered epistemic state without determining the exact state algebra; (3) state continuity can exist without state memory (continuity != memory != observability), suggesting a distinction between current state, historical continuity, accessible history, and authoritative history, classified [LENS]/[HYPOTHESIS] not ratified architecture; (4) condition-triggered intervention (a governance trigger pattern: Guard(s)=true => Remediation(s)), with the explicit warning not to jump from the narrative directly to an architecture rule -- test whether KnowledgeOS already contains the same structural pattern first; (5) action, inaction, and forbidden action are different states (not a Boolean), informing the open question OQ-4 via Execution != Consequence and ObservedActivity != ActionSemantics; (6) knowledge changes the meaning of action (MeaningOfAction(x | KnowledgeState), i.e. action is context-dependent, not semantically isolated); (7) knowledge acquisition has a protocol (a governed relationship of trust/inquiry/transformation, reinforcing an existing Extraction != Determination finding, R1); (8) doubt should be a first-class object (Doubt_t = f(K_t, Evidence_t, Contradiction_t, Requirement_t), explicitly marked as a research hypothesis, not to be added to the architecture yet); (9) knowledge and action form a closed loop (K_t -> Z_t -> Proposal -> Decision -> Authorization -> Action -> Observation -> K_{t+1}), used as a comparative validation lens for an already-existing loop rather than as new architecture.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Krishna → Lord Lens ... That's too strong. A safer mapping is: Gītā concept → structural property → abstract pattern → possible KnowledgeOS correspondence
a_rows_sample.statement: S1321's direct character-to-variable mappings (Krishna -> Lord Lens, Arjuna -> Knower, made at the very beginning of that document) are judged too strong a jump from theological/metaphysical claim straight to software variable, skipping an intermediate abstraction level. A safer four-step mapping discipline is proposed: Gita concept -> structural property (observed in text) -> abstract pattern (generalized) -> possible KnowledgeOS correspondence (candidate) -- rather than Gita concept -> mathematical equation -> KnowledgeOS architecture directly. Example: Krishna's intentional manifestation does not directly imply 'Lord = generator operator'; instead, 'the narrative distinguishes an agent that knowingly intervenes under a purpose and condition,' studied as a structural analogue of purpose-conditioned intervention.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Chapter 4 can function as an **independent stress-test lens**. That is more valuable than trying to make it a source of architecture.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes going one step further than the corrective ruling: rather than treating Chapter 4 as failing to derive the architecture, use it as an independent stress-test lens, pairing eight existing KnowledgeOS concepts with a Chapter-4-derived stress question each: K_t (can state continuity exist without complete memory?); X_t != Observed(X_t) (can history exist without present observability?); Evidence (can multiple transmission paths remain distinguishable?); Determination (what transforms transmitted information into accepted knowledge?); Authorization (what distinguishes knowing an action from being entitled to perform it?); Action (is action semantics independent of physical execution?); Governance (what triggers intervention when the current state diverges from intended order?); OQ-4 (can execution/consequence be modelled separately from action intent?). This use is judged stronger than treating the text as either a source of architecture or a failed derivation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: We should not ask: "What KnowledgeOS object corresponds to Krishna, Arjuna, Guru, etc.?" We should ask: **"What philosophical principle is expressed here, and what does that principle teach us about KnowledgeOS?"**
a_rows_sample.statement: Establishes a five-step philosophical interpretation method for using Chapter 4 (or any theological source) as KnowledgeOS research input, replacing character-to-object mapping: (1) extract the philosophical principle, not names/mythology/literal narrative (e.g. 'knowledge should produce discrimination between action and non-action'); (2) generalize the principle, removing Gita-specific theological context while preserving the underlying idea (e.g. 'a knowledge-bearing system needs discernment concerning possible actions'); (3) compare with KnowledgeOS, asking whether an existing mechanism already expresses the principle (e.g. K_t -> Zero -> Proposal -> Decision as a candidate correspondence); (4) stress-test it, asking a sharper question than simple mapping (e.g. does the current model really distinguish 'what can be done' from 'what should be done'); (5) classify the result into one of five outcomes: CONVERGENT (philosophy independently expresses something already present), REFINING (suggests a distinction the architecture should examine), NEW HYPOTHESIS (introduces a potentially useful concept), NOT APPLICABLE (philosophically interesting but architecturally irrelevant), or CONTRASTING (the philosophical principle exposes a tension with the current model).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Chapter 1: THE CRISIS ... Chapter 2: THE FRAME ... Chapter 3: THE ACTION SYSTEM ... Chapter 4: THE KNOWLEDGE-ACTION TRANSFORMATION ... This sequence suggests that a KnowledgeOS system should begin with: Problem → Purpose → Knowledge Requirement, not: Data → Knowledge
a_rows_sample.statement: Formally accepts a shift from 'mapping' (what Gita concept maps to what KnowledgeOS object) to 'testing' (what theory of knowledge/action/decision/responsibility/state/transformation emerges from the text, tested against the architecture). Chapters 1-4 are read as a coherent progression mirroring the KnowledgeOS lifecycle: Chapter 1 the crisis ('I do not know what I should do'), Chapter 2 the frame (nature of self/duty/knowledge/disciplined action), Chapter 3 the action system (interdependence/duty/consequence/responsibility), Chapter 4 the knowledge-action transformation (how knowledge changes the meaning and consequence of action). This progression is read as suggesting a KnowledgeOS system should begin with Problem -> Purpose -> Knowledge Requirement rather than Data -> Knowledge, strengthening the existing architecture's roles (Knower=entity with a problem, Purpose=what must be determined, IdealState=what would constitute resolution, KnowledgeState=what is currently known, Zero=what remains unresolved, Lord=what might be relevant, Sarathi=what action follows).

a_rows_sample.anchor: D14. step-025f (183529) -- Governance Conflict Algebra ... section14-15 authority is a PARTIAL ORDER, not a hierarchy ... section18-20 the crucial boundary: equal authority + no precedence => Resolve=Unresolved => UnresolvedGovernanceConflict -> HumanGovernance. This is not a failure ... it is the correct computational result.
a_rows_sample.statement: Step-025f (file 183529) states Conflict != Error with seven legitimate causes, requires scope-then-temporal-then-conclusion resolution of any apparent conflict, and defines Resolve(s1,s2,C,t) in {s1 wins, s2 wins, both coexist, exception, superseded, unresolved}; distinguishes HistoricalConflict != CurrentConflict; treats an exception as SatisfiedByException without deleting the original requirement; distinguishes Instruction from AuthorizedDecision, noting an AI output cannot directly override governance; establishes that authority is a context-dependent PARTIAL ORDER rather than a total hierarchy (a security policy dominates for security propositions, an architecture constitution dominates for structural ones); defines GovernanceResolve(C,S,t) -> GR=(EffectiveRules,Conflicts,Exceptions,Supersessions,UnresolvedItems); establishes the crucial boundary that equal authority with no precedence rule yields Resolve=Unresolved, routed to human governance -- explicitly stated as 'not a failure of KnowledgeOS' but 'the correct computational result', i.e. that knowing something cannot be determined is itself a valid computed result; and runs a computability sub-thesis distinguishing kernel-computable operations (graph traversal, indexing, rule evaluation, dependency resolution, version comparison, hashing) from expensive/external ones (LLM inference, large-scale semantic indexing, Monte Carlo, complex optimization), concluding the kernel needs no extraordinary computing power and the real bottleneck is semantic precision.

b_rows_sample.statement: The fundamental motivating example: a Constitution requiring Architecture Board approval for production changes conflicts with an old ADR saying approval is not required; naively collecting both as 'approval = true + false' is rejected — the system must determine whether the contradiction is resolvable by the governance model.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Conflict \neq Error
b_rows_sample.statement: First principle: two contradicting statements are not automatically an error — they may (1) have one superseding the other, (2) apply to different scopes, (3) apply at different times, (4) involve an exception, (5) reflect different authority, (6) have one simply invalid, or (7) reflect genuine unresolved governance conflict. Therefore Conflict ≠ Error; conflict is 'an input state requiring resolution.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Scope(A)\cap Scope(B)=\varnothing \Rightarrow Conflict(A,B)=False
b_rows_sample.statement: Scope precedes conflict: Policy_A:r for Production and Policy_B:¬r for Development do not conflict because Scope(A)∩Scope(B)=∅, giving the governance rule: before resolving contradiction, determine whether the propositions actually apply to the same context.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Policy_A: r, t<2026 ... Policy_B: \neg r, t\ge 2026 ... Conflict=False
b_rows_sample.statement: Temporal applicability similarly dissolves apparent conflict: time-disjoint policies produce Conflict=False for any given evaluation time t; conflict detection must first evaluate Applicable(s,C,t).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Conflict(s_1,s_2,C,t) ... Applicable(s_1,C,t) and Applicable(s_2,C,t) and Conclusion(s_1)\neq Conclusion(s_2)
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines effective conflict formally: Conflict(s1,s2,C,t) holds only when both sources are Applicable(.,C,t) and their Conclusions differ — described as 'much cleaner' than a naive contradiction check.

type_signature.domain: Source x Source x Context x Time

b_rows_sample.anchor: Resolve(s_1,s_2,C,t) ... {s1 wins, s2 wins, both coexist, exception, superseded, unresolved}
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a resolution relation Resolve(s1,s2,C,t) with six possible outcome categories: s1 wins, s2 wins, both coexist, exception, superseded, unresolved.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ADR_1\vdash r ... ADR_2\vdash\neg r ... ADR_2 supersedes ADR_1 ... Effective(ADR_1)=False ... HistoricalConflict\neq CurrentConflict
b_rows_sample.statement: Supersession example: when ADR_2 explicitly supersedes ADR_1, Effective(ADR_1)=False, so there is no active contradiction — the historical contradiction remains in KnowledgeOS history but 'does not contaminate current governance,' giving HistoricalConflict ≠ CurrentConflict.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Exception(r,C) ... r=True and ExceptionApplied=True ... SatisfiedByException
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicit exception handling: an authorized exception to a Constitution-required r should not delete r; instead the system records r=True and ExceptionApplied=True, giving state SatisfiedByException — 'preserves both the rule and the deviation.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Requirement: Architecture approval required -> deleted because someone approved an exception ... destroys governance history
b_rows_sample.statement: Warns that silently deleting a requirement upon exception approval 'destroys governance history'; shows the correct representation retains the Requirement plus an Exception record (approver, scope, validity date) so the system can explain exactly why the normal requirement was not enforced in the ordinary way.

b_rows_sample.anchor: HumanInstruction\vdash\neg r ... Authority(HumanInstruction)<Authority(Constitution) ... EffectiveConclusion=r ... Rejected/NonBinding
b_rows_sample.statement: If an unauthorized human instruction contradicts the Constitution and Authority(HumanInstruction) < Authority(Constitution), the EffectiveConclusion remains r and the human instruction becomes Rejected/NonBinding (though it should remain recorded).

b_rows_sample.anchor: HumanDecision\rightarrow AuthorizedException ... Instruction ... AuthorizedDecision
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes two semantic categories of 'human instruction': a mere Instruction versus an AuthorizedDecision from an authorized governance authority explicitly granting an exception (HumanDecision -> AuthorizedException), showing 'human instruction' is not one uniform category.

b_rows_sample.anchor: AIOutput\vdash\neg r ... Binding(AIOutput)=False ... AIOutput cannot directly override governance
b_rows_sample.statement: AI-generated governance claims (e.g. an LLM asserting an approval is unnecessary) are not binding unless backed by an authoritative source and accepted through the governance mechanism: Binding(AIOutput)=False, and 'AIOutput cannot directly override governance' — 'a fundamental KnowledgeOS invariant.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: GovernanceResolve(C,S,t)\rightarrow GR ... GR=(EffectiveRules,Conflicts,Exceptions,Supersessions,UnresolvedItems)
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the formal governance-resolution function GovernanceResolve(Context,Sources,time) -> GR, where GR is a five-component result tuple: EffectiveRules, Conflicts, Exceptions, Supersessions, UnresolvedItems.

b_rows_sample.anchor: S=\{Constitution,ADR_17,Policy_4,Exception_2\} ... Step1..Step7
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked example walking a seven-step engine process (determine applicability; normalize propositions; detect contradictions; apply supersession; apply authority; apply authorized exceptions; produce effective rules), described as 'computationally straightforward provided the governance semantics are explicitly modeled.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Suppose two equally authoritative sources say r and \neg r. No precedence exists ... Resolve=Unresolved ... KnowledgeOS must not invent an answer
b_rows_sample.statement: The crucial boundary case: when two equally authoritative sources genuinely conflict with no precedence, Resolve=Unresolved and 'KnowledgeOS must not invent an answer' — therefore UnresolvedGovernanceConflict -> HumanGovernance, explicitly stated as 'not a failure of KnowledgeOS' but 'the correct computational result.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: whether the conflict is computationally resolvable ... Knowing that something cannot be determined is itself a valid computed result
b_rows_sample.statement: States what is called 'one of the most important conclusions so far': the kernel's job is not to solve every semantic conflict but to determine whether the conflict is computationally resolvable (Resolve if yes, Escalate if no) — 'Knowing that something cannot be determined is itself a valid computed result,' framed as a principle that 'will become important throughout the architecture.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Resolved / Unresolved / Invalid
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines three fundamental governance-resolution outcome states: Resolved (a deterministic precedence/exception rule exists), Unresolved (valid sources conflict with no resolution mechanism), Invalid (a source or rule cannot legally/semantically participate).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Constitution: ProductionChange=>ArchitectureApproval ... ADR: NexusChange=>NoApproval ... GovernanceStatus=Unresolved ... Zero becomes ArchitectureApproval=Conflicted ... Lord should not guess
b_rows_sample.statement: Full worked example with no supersession/exception/scope-or-time distinction: GovernanceStatus=Unresolved, so Zero reports ArchitectureApproval=Conflicted, and Lord 'should not guess' — instead it generates the action ResolveGovernanceConflict.

b_rows_sample.anchor: GovernanceResolve(S, Context, Time): 1..9 steps
b_rows_sample.statement: Presents the full nine-step GovernanceResolve algorithm (filter by applicability; resolve versions; remove superseded; normalize propositions; detect contradictory conclusions; apply authority; apply authorized exceptions; determine effective rules; return unresolved conflicts) and states 'the difficult part is not computational complexity... it is making the semantics explicit.'
