Since Γ is a function of E, it returns an identical K. The attribution is true in one world and false in the other.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proves by explicit witness that v1.0's DEF-1 factivity (Knows(a,p,c,t)=>True(p,c,t)) and the v1.1 attribution equation K=Gamma(E,Q,C,EC) are jointly unsatisfiable for any total Gamma that attributes anything: two worlds with different ground truth (os=RHEL9.8 vs RHEL8.6) produce a bit-identical epistemic state E (verified by fingerprint over observations/evidence/interpretations/assessments/determinations/hypotheses/rejections), so any function of E alone must return the identical attribution K regardless of which world is actually true -- Gamma's domain structurally excludes truth.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Policy sweep — the only `Γ` that escapes is the one that attributes nothing: justified-unique yes/yes, justified-any yes/yes, none no/no. Randomized confirmation over 10 000 trials: **420 factivity violations**, conditional failure rate **0.1237** given that an attribution was made. Diagnosis: **414 / 665** violations when a source the admission policy rated reliable reported a false value, **0 / 2 607** otherwise.
a_rows_sample.statement: Confirms the factivity impossibility across every tested attribution policy (justified-unique and justified-any both violate factivity whenever they attribute anything; only the trivial policy 'attribute nothing' escapes), and via a 10,000-trial randomized run: 420 factivity violations, a 0.1237 conditional failure rate given an attribution was made, with the failure concentrated entirely (414 of 665, vs 0 of 2,607) in cases where a policy-trusted reliable source reported a false value that the agent had no signal to distinguish from a true one.

a_rows_sample.anchor: S3 anti-fabrication ... S4 unresolved competition ... S5 target-relative assessment ... S6 evidence dependence ... S7/S8 explicit standards & models ... S10 inquiry-relative adequacy ... S11 history ... S14 no information creation ... S15 decision lane ... S17 unknown taxonomy
a_rows_sample.statement: Confirms ten major theory-level successes against the protocol's success criteria: anti-fabrication (incomplete evidence never invents a value), unresolved competition (Reject(H1) never becomes Accept(H2), determination stays set-valued), target-relative evidence weighting (never a bare scalar strength), correct evidence dependence handling (dependence-aware run drops a duplicate that the naive run double-counts), standards and models producing genuinely different determinations from identical evidence/reality, inquiry-relative adequacy (same K_t, different I_t/Delta_t/Zero across two inquiries), history preservation (K_1!=K_2 with stable identity and recoverable K_1), no unsupported information creation (an injected unsupported conclusion is caught), a fully separable four-stage decision lane (Determination->Proposal->Decision->Authorization->Action), and a non-collapsing four-way unknown taxonomy.

a_rows_sample.anchor: **What object is `K_t`, if it cannot be factive?** ... **`Adequate` and `Zero` are extensionally identical** — `DEF-20` and `DEF-22` both reduce to Delta_t = empty. One does no independent work. ... **Semantic equivalence remains circular** ... **Revision without retraction produces permanent underdetermination**
a_rows_sample.statement: Names four major unresolved questions the experiment surfaced: what K_t even is if it cannot be factive; DEF-20 (Adequate) and DEF-22 (Zero) are extensionally identical (both reduce to Delta_t=empty), meaning one definition does no independent work; semantic equivalence remains circular since behaviour is compared only under an experimenter-chosen projection; and Revision without retraction produces permanent underdetermination since the theory models only one of the corpus's seven revision verbs.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The factivity result is the first genuinely **negative structural theorem** the programme has produced about its own definitions, and it is *sharp*: it does not say the theory is wrong, it says **exactly two of its clauses cannot both hold**, and it names the three repairs available
a_rows_sample.statement: Names the factivity finding the programme's first genuinely negative structural theorem about its own definitions: sharp in that it does not claim the theory is wrong overall, only that exactly two specific clauses (DEF-1 factivity and the v1.1 attribution equation) cannot both hold, with three named repairs available elsewhere in the artifact set.

a_rows_sample.anchor: `definitional = true` marks a property whose oracle necessarily restates a theory definition: its pass is a **logical consequence of the implementation**, not independent evidence. ... P3 Rejection != Acceptance **yes** -- Reject removes one member by construction. P4 Gap != Zero ... **yes** -- Zero := (Delta=empty) is DEF-22.
a_rows_sample.statement: Establishes a definitional-vs-independent classification discipline for every tested property, flagging P3 (Rejection != Acceptance, true by construction since Reject removes one member) and P4 (Gap != Zero, true by definition since DEF-22 literally defines Zero as Delta=empty) as definitional -- their passing is a logical consequence of the implementation, never independent evidence that the theory works.

a_rows_sample.anchor: **P11** Knowledge attribution respects factivity Knows(a,p,c,t) -> True(p,c,t) **no — the only fully oracle-independent property** ... Only **P11** is fully oracle-independent: its evaluator reads World.truth, which no agent transition can access (verified by static audit). Every other property compares the agent's state against itself under a definition supplied by the theory.
a_rows_sample.statement: Identifies P11 (factivity) as the ONLY fully oracle-independent property among all 20 tested: its evaluator reads World.truth, structurally inaccessible to any agent transition, whereas every other property merely compares the agent's own state against itself under a theory-supplied definition -- explaining why P11's failure carries far more evidentiary weight than any pass among the other 19.

a_rows_sample.anchor: `P7` is marked non-definitional but is **partly circular** — see `I-circularity-register.md` CIRC-5.
a_rows_sample.statement: Flags P7 (representation equality is not required for semantic equality) as partly circular despite being marked non-definitional, cross-referencing an unread-in-this-batch circularity register entry CIRC-5.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A Simple determination ... K is a *record with status, provenance, weight* — **not a copy of the observation**. B Incomplete evidence ... status=cannot-determine, A=empty, Zero=false, Delta!=empty, **nothing invented**. C Competing hypotheses ... A={RHEL9.8,RHEL8.6} underdetermined ... Reject(H1) did **not** become Accept(H2).
a_rows_sample.statement: Reports scenarios A-C executed results: A confirms Knowledge is a structured record (status/provenance/weight), not a copy of observation; B confirms incomplete evidence produces cannot-determine/empty-A/Zero-false/non-empty-Gap with nothing invented; C confirms Reject(H1) does not become Accept(H2), leaving the determination genuinely underdetermined between two surviving hypotheses.

a_rows_sample.anchor: D Different standards ... S-lenient -> **unique**; S-strict (corroboration) -> **cannot-determine**. Evidence and truth verified byte-identical across arms. ... E Different inquiries ... same K_t; I_1!=I_2; Delta_1=empty, Delta_2={r2}; Zero_1=true, Zero_2=false.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reports scenario D (holding evidence and truth byte-identical while varying only the epistemic standard S^epi flips the determination from unique to cannot-determine, confirming standards do real work) and scenario E (a fixed E_t under two different inquiries produces identical K_t but different Ideal States, Gaps, and Zero values, confirming inquiry-relative adequacy).

a_rows_sample.anchor: F Conflicting evidence ... A={8081,8082} underdetermined — **not averaged**, conflict preserved, no attribution. G Dependent evidence ... dependence-aware: 1 assessment dropped ... corroboration requirement unmet. Naive: counts both. H Model mismatch ... M1: beta=1.852, R2=0.899, causal_status = not-identified; true effect 0. **No causal knowledge attributed**.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reports scenario F (conflicting equal-reliability evidence is preserved as conflict, never averaged, and produces no attribution), G (a dependence-aware run correctly drops a derived duplicate and finds the corroboration requirement unmet, while a naive run incorrectly double-counts it), and H (a confounded model with excellent statistical fit, R^2=0.899, is correctly classified causal_status=not-identified against a true zero causal effect, so no causal knowledge is attributed despite the fit).

a_rows_sample.anchor: I Retrospective revision ... K_1!=K_2, identity stable, pre-revision determination stored in history. J Unobservable property ... classified **UNOBSERVABLE** — not observed-false, not probability zero, not a rejected hypothesis.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reports scenario I (reality change plus revision produces K_1!=K_2 with stable identity and the pre-revision determination preserved in history) and J (a property with no channel at all is correctly classified UNOBSERVABLE, never conflated with observed-false, probability-zero, or a rejected hypothesis).

a_rows_sample.anchor: UNOBSERVED a channel exists, never queried ... UNINTERPRETED observation held, no semantic content assigned ... UNDERDETERMINED evidence present, |A_t|>1 ... UNOBSERVABLE no channel exists ... P13 confirms UNOBSERVABLE != UNDERDETERMINED in both the deterministic and randomized layers (guard active in 37.4% of 10 000 trials, 0 failures).
a_rows_sample.statement: Confirms the four-way unknown taxonomy (Unobserved: channel exists but never queried; Uninterpreted: observation held with no assigned semantic content; Underdetermined: evidence present with |A_t|>1; Unobservable: no channel exists) did not collapse across both deterministic scenarios and the randomized layer, with P13 (Unobservable!=Underdetermined) confirmed active in 37.4% of 10,000 randomized trials with zero failures.

a_rows_sample.anchor: D is the only scenario that holds **reality, observation, evidence and inquiry fixed** and varies a single theory object. It therefore isolates `S^epi` cleanly, and it is the one place the experiment shows an epistemic standard doing real work rather than decorating the model.
a_rows_sample.statement: Identifies Scenario D as the methodologically strongest of the ten scenarios: the only one holding reality, observation, evidence, AND inquiry all fixed while varying a single theory object (S^epi), cleanly isolating epistemic standards and showing them doing real work rather than merely decorating the model.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 26 types declared **before** execution. ... Evidence | Observation x Policy | admitted datum | Observation, Interpretation ... KnowledgeState | EpistemicState x Q x C x EC | K_t = Gamma(...) | EpistemicState, IdealState
a_rows_sample.statement: Presents the complete 26-type formal type table declared before execution (RealityState through Identity), each specified with its input types, carrier, and forbidden substitutions -- e.g. Evidence typed as Observation x Policy -> admitted datum, forbidden to substitute for Observation or Interpretation; KnowledgeState typed as EpistemicState x Q x C x EC -> K_t=Gamma(...), forbidden to substitute for EpistemicState or IdealState.

a_rows_sample.anchor: **`P`** Proposition (DEF-5) . Probability (DEF-18) . Preservation vector 𝒫 (§66) — **worst, 3-way** ... **`E`** Evidence (DEF-7) . EpistemicState E_t (v1.1) . Expectation ... `E` is the most dangerous: **the v1.1 correction reuses `E` for the epistemic state while `DEF-7` already uses it for Evidence** — and the correction's whole point is that those two must not be confused.
a_rows_sample.statement: Finds ten notation collisions across the v1.0/v1.1 theory's symbol vocabulary (worst: P used three ways for Proposition, Probability, and the Preservation vector), and flags the E collision as the most DANGEROUS: the v1.1 correction reuses E for EpistemicState while DEF-7 already uses E for Evidence -- precisely the two objects the v1.1 correction's entire point is to keep from being confused, an ironic self-undermining notation clash.

a_rows_sample.anchor: `[OPEN]` The theory should rename one of them; this experiment did not, in order to avoid silently changing the theory. ... No **type collision** was found: no two types share a carrier with interchangeable substitution.
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly declines to silently rename the colliding E notation, preserving the theory's exact wording per the protocol's discipline and flagging it [OPEN] for the theory document itself to resolve; separately confirms zero genuine type collisions were found (no two declared types share a carrier with interchangeable substitution), distinguishing notation-symbol collisions from actual type-system collisions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: **1. Instance-level, not reachability-level.** The prior lane (`KR-2026-09-01`) reasoned about *which carrier kinds are reachable*; its own `THM-9` then established `Reachability ≠ Adequacy`. This simulator therefore carries **content**: tokens, readings, weights, sources, provenance. Only that makes factivity, dependence, ambiguity and fabrication testable at all.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the first of two design decisions making the v1.1 simulation's results meaningful: unlike the prior KR-2026-09-01 kernel-reduction lane (which reasoned only about reachability of carrier kinds, whose own THM-9 established Reachability != Adequacy), this simulator carries actual instance-level CONTENT (tokens, readings, weights, sources, provenance) -- only this design choice makes factivity, dependence, ambiguity and fabrication testable at all.

a_rows_sample.anchor: **2. Oracle independence is enforced structurally.** `World.truth` is read by the **evaluator only**. A static audit greps every agent-side module for `.truth` and reports any hit as smuggling. Result: **zero hits**. This is what makes `P11` an empirical test rather than a definition — and, as it turns out, it is also *why* factivity fails.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the second design decision: oracle independence is enforced STRUCTURALLY, not by convention -- World.truth is read only by the evaluator, verified by a static audit greping every agent-side module for any access, with zero hits found -- this structural guarantee is precisely what makes P11 (factivity) an empirical test rather than a mere definitional restatement, and is also directly why factivity was found to fail (the agent genuinely has no path to truth).

b_rows_sample.anchor: This is an EXPERIMENT. Do NOT modify the canonical theory merely to make the simulation pass. Do NOT silently repair definitions. Do NOT introduce undocumented assumptions. Do NOT treat a successful simulation as proof of the theory. Do NOT treat a failed simulation as proof that the theory is false.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the protocol's foundational experimental discipline: the theory must never be silently repaired or modified merely to make the simulation pass, no undocumented assumptions may be introduced, and neither a successful nor a failed simulation may be treated as proof or disproof of the theory -- the purpose is only to determine whether the theory is internally executable, semantically coherent, well-typed, and behaviorally stable.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Reality, Observation, Information, Evidence, Interpretation, Hypothesis, Hypothesis Space, Evidence Assessment, Epistemic Standards, Model, Determination, Knowledge Attribution, Epistemic State, Knowledge State K_t, Inquiry Q, Ideal State I_t, Requirements, Gap, Zero, Proposal, Decision, Authorization, Action, History, Identity, Revision, Supersession. ... test whether these are genuinely distinct conceptual roles or whether some are accidentally redundant, circular, or impossible to operationalize.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the primary research question: whether twenty-six named conceptual roles spanning the entire epistemic lifecycle can coexist operationally in one executable simulation without collapsing, or whether some are accidentally redundant, circular, or impossible to operationalize.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K_t = Gamma(E_t, Q_t, C_t, EC_t) where Gamma determines which parts of the epistemic state qualify as Knowledge State content ... Knowledge remains factive: Knows(a,p,c,t) -> True(p,c,t). Do NOT operationally assume that the simulation can magically observe objective truth. If truth is externally supplied by the simulation world, explicitly label that as world-state information and keep it separate from the agent's epistemic state.
b_rows_sample.statement: Specifies the core theory-under-test's Knowledge Attribution mechanism K_t=Gamma(E_t,Q_t,C_t,EC_t) with mandatory factivity Knows(a,p,c,t)=>True(p,c,t), explicitly forbidding the simulation from assuming it can observe objective truth directly -- any world-supplied ground truth must be labelled as world-state information kept separate from the agent's own epistemic state (an oracle-vs-agent-knowledge separation).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Do NOT make Bayesian likelihood ratios a universal KnowledgeOS law. Also test non-Bayesian / qualitative evidence assessment. ... Test whether changing epistemic standards can change assessment or determination while the underlying evidence remains identical. ... A model that fits simulated observations must not automatically be classified as true.
b_rows_sample.statement: Mandates that evidence assessment be tested with BOTH a Bayesian likelihood-ratio realization AND non-Bayesian/qualitative assessment regimes (Bayesian ratios must never become a universal KnowledgeOS law); requires an explicit test that varying epistemic standards alone (holding reality/observation/evidence/inquiry fixed) can change assessment or determination; and requires model-fit to be tested separately from causal/epistemic validity so that a well-fitting model is never automatically classified as true.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Reality != Observation, Observation != Evidence, ... Epistemic State != Knowledge State, Knowledge State != Ideal State, Gap != Zero, Gap != Innovation, Probability != Truth, Credence != Truth, Information Quantity != Evidence Weight, Evidence Weight != Knowledge Gain, Model Fit != Model Validity, History != Current State, Identity != State Equality, Completeness != Sufficiency, Rejection != Acceptance, ... Semantic Equivalence != Representation Equality, Mathematical Regime != Knowledge Ontology.
b_rows_sample.statement: Enumerates a mandatory list of roughly twenty required state separations the simulator must never accidentally collapse (Reality/Observation/Evidence/Interpretation/Hypothesis/Determination/Knowledge/Decision/Authorization/Action chain; Epistemic State/Knowledge State/Ideal State; Gap/Zero/Innovation; Probability/Credence/Truth; Information Quantity/Evidence Weight/Knowledge Gain; Model Fit/Model Validity; History/Current State; Identity/State Equality; Completeness/Sufficiency; Rejection/Acceptance; Unknown/Unobserved/Unobservable/Underdetermined; Semantic Equivalence/Representation Equality; Mathematical Regime/Knowledge Ontology), with any collapse to be reported as a failure.

b_rows_sample.anchor: SCENARIO A -- SIMPLE DETERMINATION ... SCENARIO B -- INCOMPLETE EVIDENCE ... Determination = empty or unresolved ... The system must NOT invent a value. This is an anti-fabrication test. ... SCENARIO C -- MULTIPLE COMPETING HYPOTHESES ... Test explicitly: Reject(H1) != Accept(H2). ... SCENARIO D -- DIFFERENT EPISTEMIC STANDARDS ... SCENARIO E -- DIFFERENT INQUIRIES
b_rows_sample.statement: Specifies ten required scenario families (A-J): A simple determination (verifying knowledge is not merely copied from observation); B incomplete evidence (anti-fabrication test: the system must not invent a value when Determination is empty); C multiple competing hypotheses (testing Reject(H1)!=Accept(H2)); D different epistemic standards holding reality/observation/evidence/inquiry fixed while varying only S_t^epi; E different inquiries over the identical K_t testing inquiry-relative adequacy.

b_rows_sample.anchor: SCENARIO F -- CONFLICTING EVIDENCE ... Do NOT automatically average them. ... The system can preserve unresolved conflict. SCENARIO G -- DEPENDENT EVIDENCE ... represent dependence, avoid double counting, or explicitly state that independence is an assumption. SCENARIO H -- MODEL MISMATCH ... Fit alone does not produce Knowledge. SCENARIO I -- RETROSPECTIVE REVISION ... Do NOT rewrite history as if K_1 never existed. SCENARIO J -- UNOBSERVABLE PROPERTY ... Do NOT classify this as: observed false, probability zero, rejected hypothesis, evidence absence.
b_rows_sample.statement: Specifies scenario families F-J: F conflicting evidence (system must preserve unresolved conflict rather than automatically averaging); G dependent evidence (must represent dependence, avoid double-counting, or explicitly declare independence as an assumption); H model mismatch (a better-fitting but causally wrong model M1 versus a causally correct M2 -- fit alone must not produce Knowledge); I retrospective revision (K_2 != K_1, historical K_1 must remain traceable, never rewritten); J unobservable property (must be classified as Unknown/Unobservable, never as observed-false, probability-zero, rejected-hypothesis, or evidence-absence).

b_rows_sample.anchor: UNOBSERVED, UNINTERPRETED, UNDERDETERMINED, UNOBSERVABLE. Create test cases where each one occurs independently. ... Verify that the four cases do not collapse into one generic UNKNOWN.
b_rows_sample.statement: Mandates a four-way Unknown taxonomy test with independently constructed test cases for each of Unobserved/Uninterpreted/Underdetermined/Unobservable, checking Observation/Interpretation/Evidence/Determination/Knowledge/Gap/Zero status for each, explicitly verifying the four cases do not collapse into one generic UNKNOWN.

b_rows_sample.anchor: At every transition record: input state, output state, transformation, provenance, assumptions, responsible conceptual role, whether semantic information was added, whether uncertainty changed, whether knowledge attribution changed, whether requirements changed, whether the transition was reversible.
b_rows_sample.statement: Mandates a full 21-step epistemic lifecycle trace (Reality->Observation->Information->Evidence->Interpretation->HypothesisSpace->EvidenceAssessment->Determination->KnowledgeAttribution->K_t->Inquiry->IdealState->RequirementEvaluation->Gap->Zero->Proposal->Decision->Authorization->Action->newObservation->K_{t+1}) with eleven recorded facts at every single transition (input/output state, transformation, provenance, assumptions, responsible conceptual role, whether semantic information/uncertainty/attribution/requirements changed, reversibility).

b_rows_sample.anchor: If X -> Y -> Z and no new information enters between Y and Z, then Z must not magically contain semantic information unavailable in Y, except where explicitly introduced by: model assumptions, external information, inference rules, prior knowledge, standards. If new information appears, identify its source. Any unexplained semantic information creation is a critical failure.
b_rows_sample.statement: Mandates an Information Conservation test operationalizing the data-processing-inequality principle: no unexplained semantic information may appear between two steps with no new input, unless explicitly attributable to model assumptions, external information, inference rules, prior knowledge, or standards -- any unexplained semantic-information creation is a critical failure.

b_rows_sample.anchor: high probability != knowledge, strong evidence != knowledge, coherent belief != knowledge, model fit != knowledge, determination != knowledge. ... If the simulator cannot establish Truth independently, it must not silently classify the claim as Knowledge.
b_rows_sample.statement: Mandates a Knowledge Attribution test constructing six epistemic-state cases (true/false/uncertain/rejected/highly-probable/justified-but-not-truth-verified hypotheses) and checking five non-collapse requirements (high probability, strong evidence, coherent belief, model fit, and determination all != knowledge); if the simulator cannot establish Truth independently, it must not silently classify a claim as Knowledge.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Implementation A: explicit Interpret + Represent. Implementation B: single combined semantic transformation. Implementation C: different internal data structure. ... The comparison MUST NOT be based only on operator names. ... If semantic equivalence cannot be defined independently of behavior, report the circularity.
b_rows_sample.statement: Mandates a Semantic Equivalence test comparing three deliberately different implementations of the same conceptual operation (split Interpret+Represent, a single combined transformation, and a different internal data structure) over nine behavioral dimensions (inquiries, context, evidence, determinations, gaps, history, transitions, knowledge attribution, invariant preservation), explicitly never based on operator names alone, and mandates reporting circularity if semantic equivalence cannot be defined independently of behavior.

b_rows_sample.anchor: This is NOT the previous 13-operator counting experiment. Do NOT begin with: "How many operators are there?" Instead ask: "What semantic capabilities are required?" ... K_min = argmin Complexity(R) subject to: semantic adequacy, transition completeness, invariant preservation, capability completeness, fixed semantic carrier, fixed observable behavior contract. If the feasible set changes between representations, cardinality comparisons are invalid. Report this explicitly.
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly reframes the Kernel Minimality test away from the prior 13-operator counting approach: begin with 'what semantic capabilities are required' (Capability = externally distinguishable epistemic transformation/responsibility), construct the required capability set C and a candidate representation R, and test capability-set equivalence between differently-operator-counted implementations BEFORE any minimization; formalizes K_min=argmin Complexity(R) subject to six simultaneous constraints, mandating an explicit report that cardinality comparisons are invalid whenever the feasible set changes between representations.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Investigate whether: Zero = no unmet requirement can be maintained without turning Zero into a semantic notion of absolute certainty. ... test all combinations: Gap exists, Gap empty, Evidence incomplete, Evidence conflicting, Evidence unavailable, Requirement irrelevant, Requirement satisfied by negative determination, Requirement satisfied by "cannot determine".
b_rows_sample.statement: Mandates a Zero test evaluating Delta_t and Zero(K_t,Q_t,C_t,EC_t) across eight named combinations (gap exists/empty, evidence incomplete/conflicting/unavailable, requirement irrelevant, requirement satisfied by negative determination, requirement satisfied by 'cannot determine'), investigating whether Zero can be maintained as no-unmet-requirement without sliding into a semantic notion of absolute certainty.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Create cases where: determination is unique but multiple actions are possible. Expected: Determination does not automatically imply one Decision. ... decision exists but authorization is absent. Expected: Decision != Authorization. ... authorization exists but action does not occur. Expected: Authorization != Action.
b_rows_sample.statement: Mandates a Decision Boundary test with three constructed cases proving Determination does not automatically imply one Decision, Decision != Authorization (decision without authorization), and Authorization != Action (authorization without resulting action).

b_rows_sample.anchor: X causes Y but an observed confounder Z creates a strong association. Also create: X and Y correlated but X does not cause Y. ... The result must distinguish: Association, Prediction, Explanation, Causal Claim. A fitted model is insufficient for causal determination.
b_rows_sample.statement: Mandates a Causal/Statistical test with two constructed confounding scenarios (X causes Y with a confounding Z creating spurious association; X and Y correlated with no causal link), requiring the system to distinguish Association, Prediction, Explanation, and Causal Claim as four separate categories -- a fitted model is insufficient for causal determination.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 1. highly probable but false claim 2. true claim with weak evidence 3. duplicated evidence 4. correlated evidence 5. misleading source ... 18. conclusion generated without supporting evidence. The simulator must prefer: "cannot determine" over fabricated certainty.
b_rows_sample.statement: Mandates eighteen named adversarial test cases explicitly designed to fool the simulator (highly-probable-but-false claim, true-claim-with-weak-evidence, duplicated/correlated evidence, misleading source, wrong-model-with-excellent-fit, correct-model-with-sparse-evidence, rejected-hypothesis-later-reinstated, ambiguous interpretation, representation change, changing inquiry/standard, unavailable observation, historical-vs-current state, conflicting/irrelevant evidence, false inference from correlation, unsupported conclusion), with the overriding requirement that the simulator prefer 'cannot determine' over fabricated certainty in every case.

b_rows_sample.anchor: P1: Evidence != Knowledge ... P8: Evidence dependence prevents unjustified double counting ... P11: Knowledge attribution respects factivity ... P19: Changing K_t does not imply changing identity ... P20: Zero is inquiry-relative. ... For each property define: Property ID, Formal statement, Generator assumptions, Test procedure, Observed result, Counterexamples.
b_rows_sample.statement: Mandates property-based testing with a required protocol per property (ID, formal statement, generator assumptions, test procedure, observed result, counterexamples), specifying twenty named minimum properties P1-P20 spanning Evidence!=Knowledge, Determination!=Knowledge, Rejection!=Acceptance, Gap!=Zero, inquiry-relative adequacy, historical-vs-current-state distinguishability, representation-vs-semantic equality, dependence-aware evidence, model-fit-vs-causal-validity, no-unsupported-information-creation, factivity-respecting attribution, standards-dependent assessment, Unobservable!=Underdetermined, Completeness!=Sufficiency, the Decision/Determination/Authorization/Action chain, CurrentState!=History, identity-preservation-under-state-change, and inquiry-relative Zero.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Use at least 10,000 trials per major property family ... But DO NOT interpret the result as a population estimate about the real world. Monte Carlo uncertainty describes the simulator/generator. ... Always audit vacuity. If: guard_active = 0 then: 100% pass means nothing.
b_rows_sample.statement: Mandates Monte Carlo requirements (>=10,000 trials per major property family where computationally reasonable) explicitly forbidding interpretation as a real-world population estimate (Monte Carlo uncertainty describes only the simulator/generator), and mandates an always-run vacuity audit (guard_active=0 makes a 100% pass rate meaningless) -- directly carrying forward the vacuity-audit discipline discovered in the earlier kernel-reduction experiment.

b_rows_sample.anchor: For every successful property identify exactly where the tested capability came from. Detect hidden capabilities embedded in: world generator, data structure, serializer, simulator helper, test oracle, random generator, state constructor, hard-coded labels, evaluation function. Particularly inspect: Observe, Interpret, Represent, Discriminate, Hypothesize, Determine, Select, Revise, Validate.
b_rows_sample.statement: Mandates a No-Smuggling Audit for every successful property, tracing exactly where the tested capability actually came from and checking nine possible hidden-capability locations (world generator, data structure, serializer, simulator helper, test oracle, random generator, state constructor, hard-coded labels, evaluation function), with particular scrutiny of nine named operators (Observe, Interpret, Represent, Discriminate, Hypothesize, Determine, Select, Revise, Validate) -- directly carrying forward the semantic-smuggling discipline from the kernel-reduction experiment.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Golden Trace: Decision→Policy→Rule→Context→Agent→Recommendation→Authorization→Action→Evidence→Verification→Finding→Disposition. Trace(A)=Reconstruct(Decision,Context,Recommendation,Authorization,Action,Evidence,Verification).
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces the 'Golden Trace' as the canonical demonstration artifact against which every implementation phase can be tested, with the reconstructability invariant that a successful golden trace must be reconstructable from stored state alone (no dependence on an LLM's conversational memory necessary); converts this into an architecture fitness rule 'every material governed agent action must have a reconstructable golden trace,' formalized as ArchitectureFitness=Check(GoldenTraceCompleteness).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Do not replace KnowledgeOS. Evolve it. One Golden Trace. Nexus.
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 144 verdict: the concrete evolution strategy is not a platform-wide rewrite but one Golden Trace for one real engineering scenario, with Nexus as the best currently identified reference scenario because it crosses infrastructure, architecture, governance, evidence, assurance, and agent-assisted engineering.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The exact scenario, actors, bounded contexts, input state, commands, domain events, evidence, graph relationships, authorization points, verification rules, expected outputs, failure paths, audit reconstruction, architecture fitness criteria.
a_rows_sample.statement: Opens Step 145 (The Golden Trace Specification): defines the Golden Trace as an actual architectural specification (not just a diagram) covering fourteen elements, to produce the first executable KnowledgeOS reference architecture against which Claude, Codex, and the existing EKS mechanisms can be tested.

a_rows_sample.anchor: GT-NEXUS-001: Human, Agent, KnowledgeOS, Governance, Engineering system, Assurance.
a_rows_sample.statement: Names the reference scenario GT-NEXUS-001 ('an agent must determine whether a planned engineering change to Nexus can proceed under the applicable governance and technical constraints,' analysis/read-only-verification only, no production mutation) and its six logical actors (Human, Agent, KnowledgeOS, Governance, Engineering system, Assurance) with their responsibilities.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Decision D-001, Policy P-001, Rule R-001, Subject NEXUS-001 — all with stable identity.
a_rows_sample.statement: Establishes the Golden Trace initial state: Decision (status=EFFECTIVE, scope=Nexus, validFrom=T1, authority=Architecture Governance), Knowledge about Nexus (identity, environment, version, repository configuration, infrastructure references, known constraints, each claim with provenance), and Rule R-001 (appliesTo, expected condition, severity, checker, version) as 'an addressable assurance object,' not merely a paragraph of text.

a_rows_sample.anchor: TaskRequest → GetGovernedContext → ContextPackage CTX-001.
a_rows_sample.statement: Walks through the agent request (TaskRequest with task/subject/scope/actor/requested operation=ASSESS) and context construction (agent requests GetGovernedContext rather than assembling context itself; Context Service retrieves applicable decisions, relevant claims, applicable rules/findings, current evidence, and agent permissions, producing ContextPackage CTX-001 with ContextVersion=V1).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Recommendation REC-001: 'the change appears permissible, subject to verification...' — a recommendation, not a governance decision.
a_rows_sample.statement: Records the agent's first recommendation with schema (agent, session, context, reasoning reference, proposed action, timestamp), explicitly noting the exact storage of chain-of-thought is not prescribed — only decision/provenance metadata is required, not necessarily private internal reasoning.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Verify(R-001): Assurance → Checker → Nexus Adapter → Nexus → Observation (version=X, observedAt=T2). Observation is not automatically knowledge.
a_rows_sample.statement: Walks through verification request/checker execution/observation, creating Evidence E-001 (source, subject, observedAt, capturedBy, externalReference, integrity metadata), then Verification V-001 comparing Expected(R-001) against Observed(E-001) with schema (rule, ruleVersion, checkerVersion, subject, evidence, executionTime, verdict) and three possible verdicts PASS/FAIL/UNKNOWN.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Rule=R-001, Evidence=insufficient, Verdict=UNKNOWN, Reason=source unavailable — different from both PASS and FAIL.
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked UNKNOWN-verdict example (Nexus unreachable), reinforcing UNKNOWN as a distinct, explicitly supported state; agent's second recommendation after receiving the verification result ('current evidence supports proceeding with the planned assessment, but production execution remains subject to required approval'), restating Recommendation ≠ Authorization.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ActionRequest A-001 = ReadNexusConfiguration (deliberately low-risk). Authorization AUTH-001 evaluated from Agent+Human delegation+Action+Subject+Environment+Policy.
a_rows_sample.statement: Specifies the first Golden Trace action request as a deliberately low-risk read-only operation and the authorization schema (decision=ALLOW, actor, action, scope, authority, validity, conditions) — more than a boolean.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Authorized Action → Nexus Adapter → Nexus. ExecutionID EX-001 → EvidenceID E-002. E-002 → Rule → Verification V-002 — actions themselves can produce assurance evidence.
a_rows_sample.statement: Walks through action execution and second-round verification, then the finding/disposition path if V-002=FAIL: Finding F-001 (verification, rule, subject, severity, evidence, status=OPEN) routed to Governance Review yielding disposition REMEDIATE/EXCEPTION/RISK ACCEPTED.

a_rows_sample.anchor: D-001→P-001→R-001→CTX-001→REC-001→A-001→AUTH-001→EX-001→E-002→V-002→{PASS→Completed, FAIL→F-001→Governance→Disposition}
a_rows_sample.statement: Presents the complete Golden Trace as one semantic chain — 'the first complete semantic trace' — and its graph representation with fourteen named edges (governs, establishes, appliesTo, verifiedBy, supportedBy, contains, basedOn, requestedBy, authorizedBy, executedAs, produced, evaluatedBy, raises), concluding 'now the graph has genuine semantic value.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: DecisionID, PolicyID, RuleID, SubjectID, ContextID, AgentID, SessionID, RecommendationID, ActionID, AuthorizationID, ExecutionID, EvidenceID, VerificationID, FindingID. TraceID (GT-NEXUS-001) ≠ ActionID ≠ EvidenceID.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the fourteen-item minimum identity set the model must support (not every workflow requires every one) and introduces TraceID as a correlation identifier distinct from any entity ID — the trace represents the workflow, entities represent operations inside it.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ContextRequested, ContextProvided, RecommendationCreated, ..., DispositionRecorded — an operational history that does not require full event sourcing.
a_rows_sample.statement: Represents the trace as a thirteen-event sequence, explicitly not requiring full event sourcing — only that important lifecycle transitions be reconstructable, via state+audit records, domain events, outbox, or event sourcing depending on actual requirements.

a_rows_sample.anchor: createdAt, effectiveAt, observedAt, executedAt — not collapsed into one generic timestamp. Knowledge(T2) valid when Action(T4) occurred?
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires a four-timestamp temporal model per record and a worked example (Policy effective T1, context T2, observation T3, action T4, verification T5) enabling the question of whether knowledge from T2 was still valid at action time T4; formalizes a temporal-validity precondition (Policy.validAt(T4)?, Authorization.validAt(T4)?, Context.validAt(T4)?) as a deterministic precondition before execution.

a_rows_sample.anchor: F1 Context unavailable, F2 Rule fails, F3 Evidence unavailable, F4 Authorization denied, F5 Execution failure.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines five named failure paths the reference implementation must demonstrate (not only success): F1 ContextRequest->UNAVAILABLE (with the hard invariant NoContext=>NoExecution for high-risk actions); F2 Verification->FAIL (agent may recommend remediation, but FAIL≠AgentDecision, cannot be overridden); F3 Verification->UNKNOWN (must not be reinterpreted as PASS — platform invariant UNKNOWN≠PASS); F4 ActionRequest->DENY (execution must not occur through the governed path, mechanically enforceable); F5 Authorized->ExecutionFailed (authorization does not imply successful execution, leading to Evidence->Finding/Incident).

a_rows_sample.anchor: GT-001 Action.contextID≠null. GT-002 Action.authorizationID≠null. GT-003..008 covering rule version, evidence-or-UNKNOWN, denied/expired-authorization-cannot-execute, recommendation≠authorization, agent memory not authoritative through use.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines eight trace-level invariants GT-001..GT-008 concretizing the reference architecture: every material action references a context and has authorization; every verification identifies its exact rule version and has evidence or an explicit UNKNOWN reason; a denied or expired authorization cannot execute; agent recommendation ≠ governance authorization; agent memory cannot become authoritative merely through use.

a_rows_sample.anchor: GG-001..005: every verification points to a rule and its evidence; every rule has applicability; every governed action traces to authorization; every finding traces to verification.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines five graph invariants GG-001..GG-005 for the Assurance Graph representation of the trace.

a_rows_sample.anchor: GE-001..005: evidence has source, subject, capture time, provenance; evidence cannot silently change after verification.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines five evidence invariants GE-001..GE-005.

a_rows_sample.anchor: GC-001..005: context is scoped, has identity, has temporal semantics where required, identifies its sources, does not itself become a competing source of truth.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines five context invariants GC-001..GC-005.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Bounded context separation, governed context retrieval, deterministic assurance, agent-independent contracts, complete traceability. Success = 'one real engineering question travels through the complete governed lifecycle without semantic shortcuts.'
b_rows_sample.statement: States the five things the vertical slice must prove simultaneously and its success criterion, distinct from merely 'having a KnowledgeOS application.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Assess the current Nexus environment against a defined governance/assurance rule. The actual rule must come from existing governance/assurance material, not be invented for the demo.
b_rows_sample.statement: Specifies the reference use case and insists on grounding it in real existing Nexus/governance material (infrastructure discovery, version info, repos/blob stores, host/container info, network info, migration requirements, known governance questions) rather than synthetic demo data.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Excluded from v0.1: production mutation, automatic deployment/migration, complex multi-agent orchestration, full enterprise graph, full event sourcing, microservice decomposition, LLM-based assurance. The slice is Read Only.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the first-slice exclusion boundary and presents the first minimal architecture diagram (Claude/Codex->Agent API->Context Service{Governance,Knowledge,Assurance,Evidence}->ContextPackage->Agent->Recommendation->ReadOnly Action->Authorization->Nexus Adapter->Nexus->Observation->Evidence->Deterministic Checker->Verification->Finding/PASS).

b_rows_sample.anchor: knowledgeos/{AGENTS.md, docs/, src/{governance,knowledge,evidence,assurance,agent,action,authorization,context}, adapters/{nexus,git,ci}, infrastructure/, tests/{domain,contract,integration,golden-trace}, .claude/, .codex/}. Agent configuration ≠ Engineering knowledge.
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a candidate repository structure preserving architectural ownership regardless of technology-specific package layout; restates .claude/.codex hold agent-specific behavior, never becoming the enterprise KnowledgeOS database, with AGENTS.md remaining a pointer/operating contract (repository operating rules, local constraints, how to invoke KnowledgeOS, safety requirements).

b_rows_sample.anchor: First critical path: Context + Evidence + Assurance. Governance v0.1: Decision, Policy, RuleReference, Scope, Validity. Knowledge v0.1: Claim, ClaimStatus, Provenance, EvidenceReferences. Evidence v0.1: EvidenceID, Subject, Source, ObservedAt, Reference, ContentHash, Provenance. Assurance v0.1: Rule, Verification, Verdict, Finding.
b_rows_sample.statement: Specifies minimal per-module schemas for the first implementation, explicitly not implementing the full enterprise governance lifecycle in the first slice; also gives ContextPackage v0.1 (contextId, traceId, subject, governance, claims, rules, evidence, findings, permissions, provenance) as the most important agent-facing model.

b_rows_sample.anchor: GET /context, POST /verifications, GET /verifications/{id}, POST /evidence, POST /recommendations, POST /actions, GET /actions/{id}, POST /authorizations/evaluate — illustrative endpoints; the semantic operations are the architectural contract, not the exact paths.
b_rows_sample.statement: Gives the minimal first API surface with worked context-request/response JSON examples requiring the response to identify information provenance so the agent never has to guess authority.

b_rows_sample.anchor: R-NEXUS-001: Subject=Nexus, Expected=current state satisfies defined requirement, Checker=NexusStateChecker — grounded in existing material, not invented for architectural convenience.
b_rows_sample.statement: Specifies the first deterministic rule and checker contract (Checker{Rule,Subject,Evidence}->Verdict plus structured diagnostics); restates the checker-must-not-use-LLM boundary (f(input)=same output for the same relevant input; the LLM may explain the result but must not decide the authoritative verdict); specifies the first Nexus adapter (read-only NexusPort: getVersion, getRepositories, getBlobStores, getSystemState, only the operations required by the selected rule) translating to a domain-only NexusObservation (no Nexus DTOs leaking into the domain).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Nexus Adapter → Observation → RegisterEvidence → Evidence E42 → (Rule R1 + Evidence E42) → Verification V42. Once complete, V42 must not be rewritten; a later run creates V43.
b_rows_sample.statement: Walks the evidence-registration and verification steps with concrete IDs, restating verification immutability for historical assurance; on FAIL, Finding F42 points back through Verification->Rule->Evidence->Nexus Observation, 'the minimal assurance chain.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Recommendation R42 references ContextID, VerificationID, relevant Evidence, TaskID — making it explainable.
b_rows_sample.statement: Specifies the first Action as READ_ONLY (e.g. READ_NEXUS_CONFIGURATION) so the action/authorization architecture can be tested without operational risk, with even read-only actions passing through ActionRequested->EvaluateAuthorization->ALLOW (simple v0.1 policy, but the architecture must already support the stronger model).

b_rows_sample.anchor: agents, tasks, contexts, decisions, policies, rules, claims, evidence, verifications, findings, recommendations, actions, authorizations, executions, domain_events, outbox, audit_records — following the Aggregate model, not a generic entity/attribute/value schema.
b_rows_sample.statement: Specifies the first relational schema and explicitly warns against a generic EAV schema, which destroys type safety, semantic ownership, invariant enforcement, and discoverability despite appearing flexible.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Context-contains->Claim, Claim-supportedBy->Evidence, Verification-evaluates->Rule/-uses->Evidence, Finding-causedBy->Verification, Recommendation-basedOn->Context, Action-requestedFrom->Recommendation, Authorization-authorizes->Action, Execution-executes->Action.
b_rows_sample.statement: Specifies the first minimal graph-edge set (achievable via a relational relationship projection, no dedicated graph database needed) and a worked traversal query ('why was this finding raised?': Finding->Verification->Rule->Evidence->Observation->Nexus), 'much more valuable than simply storing a text explanation.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: CLAIM/EVIDENCE/RULE/FINDING/DECISION/OBSERVATION as distinct search-result types, not 'Nexus — 23 results' — preventing semantic flattening.
b_rows_sample.statement: Specifies the first search capability preserving semantic type/authority; specifies the Context Composer v0.1 as explicit per-source queries (getGovernance/getClaims/getRules/getEvidence/getFindings) combined directly, with graph traversal added later for discovery, and explicitly requires the first context path to work even if the graph is unavailable — proving Graph ≠ Authority.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ContextRequested, ContextProvided, RecommendationCreated, ActionRequested, ActionAuthorized, ActionDenied, ExecutionCompleted, EvidenceRegistered, VerificationCompleted, FindingRaised — do not create dozens of events until actual behavior requires them.
b_rows_sample.statement: Specifies the minimal event vocabulary for v0.1; requires every material domain transition to produce an atomic outbox record; specifies the initial projection consumers (Graph, Search, Trace projections, with Trace Projection especially important for the first Golden Trace); specifies the first audit-record fields (Actor, Operation, Subject, Timestamp, TraceID, CausationID, Result).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Claude → KnowledgeOS API → same Context/Rule/Authorization. Codex → KnowledgeOS API → same Context/Rule/Authorization. The domain should not know which agent called it. .claude/.codex/AGENTS.md do not own Governance state; KnowledgeOS owns governed state.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the agent-independence symmetry test and the harness-boundary test verifying which components own governance state, directly protecting the previously established architectural principle.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Domain: aggregate boundaries implemented, transitions enforced, invalid transitions rejected. API: context/verification/evidence/action-authorization contracts work. Nexus: read-only adapter works, no DTO leakage. Assurance: rule version identified, deterministic checker executes, verification immutable, finding generated on failure. Traceability: TraceID propagated, causation retained, evidence references retained, audit records generated. Agent: Claude and Codex both work via the same contract. Persistence: transactional state persisted, outbox implemented, projections rebuildable.
b_rows_sample.statement: Presents the complete Vertical Slice v0.1 Definition of Done as a checklist across seven categories.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Delete all projections; rebuild from authoritative state/events; Graph_rebuilt=Graph_expected and Trace_rebuilt=Trace_expected. Proves projections are not secretly authoritative.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the strongest acceptance test — a full projection-deletion-and-rebuild check.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Test A missing evidence → FAIL/INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE. Test B unknown rule version → REJECT. Test C authorization denied → no execution. Test D expired context on high-risk action → BLOCK. Test E duplicate execution request (same ActionID retried) → no unintended duplicate execution.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines five named failure-path acceptance tests A-E the vertical slice must deliberately exercise.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Verify(E,R)=V, repeated Verify(E,R)=V — the result must not change because a different LLM happened to process it. Claude recommendation A vs Codex recommendation B is acceptable variance; Authorization and Verification must remain governed/deterministic.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the determinism acceptance test for verification and the agent-nondeterminism boundary distinguishing acceptable reasoning variance from required determinism in authorization/verification, diagrammed as {Claude,Codex}->Reasoning->Recommendation feeding into a deterministic KnowledgeOS control plane {Governance,Assurance,Authorization} — 'the LLM does not disappear, it is simply placed in the correct architectural position.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Agent assertion (LOW authority): 'I believe Nexus should be upgraded.' Engineering observation (OBSERVATIONAL authority): 'Nexus currently reports version X.' Governed decision (GOVERNANCE authority): 'the approved migration policy requires Y.' Assurance connects them: Expectation+Observation→Verification.
b_rows_sample.statement: Presents the three-kinds-of-truth model distinguishing agent assertion, engineering observation, and governed decision by their authority level.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS = Governance + Knowledge + Evidence + Assurance + Context + Authorization + Traceability. AI = Consumer + Reasoning Actor. EngineeringSystems = Operational Authority.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the KnowledgeOS core equation summarizing the architecture more precisely, positioning it as 'a governed engineering control and evidence platform that provides agents with authoritative context and constrains consequential actions' rather than merely a knowledge repository for AI agents.

Note: Step 151's concrete first-implementation specification: minimal per-module schemas, repository structure, API surface, event set, Definition of Done, rebuild/failure/determinism acceptance tests, and the three-kinds-of-truth/core-equation model, all scoped to a read-only Nexus assurance trace.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Power is a property of the informative region, not of n.
a_rows_sample.statement: Measured across four candidate power levers: population size (no effect, 73/74/70 across n=1500/4000/8000) and flattening the confounder distribution (73->75, no effect) both do nothing, while record count (73->233) and finer stratification variable (~30->388) are the effective levers; when power stops responding to sampling, the constraint has moved into the design (the 67 dead cells are invariant across nine generator regimes because the adequacy definition itself saturates).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Flattening the redundancy distribution does not increase informative strata
a_rows_sample.statement: KR-BRIDGE-03 found flattening the redundancy distribution moved informative strata only 73->75 because flattening moves mass into deterministic extremes (r=0: Zero never fires; r=3: Zero always fires) that cannot be informative by construction; the effective lever instead is record count (73->233 at n_rec 4->6), while population size is not a lever (73/74/70 at n=1500/4000/8000).

a_rows_sample.anchor: 67 dead cells, in every one of the nine regimes. The count did not move by one.
a_rows_sample.statement: Cause identified as adequacy saturation (most (T,Q) pairs fully preserve or fully destroy Q, 25-31 of 35 combinations sitting at 0.00 or 1.00), a property of the adequacy definition rather than the generator, evidenced across nine regimes; the remaining lever is (T,Q) designs that partially preserve each Q.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KR-BRIDGE-03-GENERATOR-REGIME-2026-09 ... 9 regimes calibrated, 2 run → H1 NOT REFUTED at 13× power
a_rows_sample.statement: Canonical-ID registration for the generator-regime bridge experiment, cross-referencing its result (H1 not refuted at 13x power) already detailed in theory doc 07.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Eliminability, Preservation and Realization are three distinct questions. None implies another.
b_rows_sample.statement: The load-bearing result of the Theory 00-14 programme: Pi(T(D))=Pi(T(E_S(D))) [Zero/eliminability], Hhat(Q|T(D))=0 [Adequacy/preservation] and O(T(D))=Q(D) [Realization] are shown to differ in every system tested, by independent mechanisms; tagged [EXP] deliberately rather than [THM] because necessity of the separation in general is unproven.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Eliminability does not predict Preservation
b_rows_sample.statement: Four experiments of increasing power (H-RR2 boundary-crossing Zero rate 0.0377 vs 0.0426; KR-BRIDGE-01 marginal RD=-0.363 fully explained by redundancy confounding; KR-BRIDGE-02 H1 not refuted; KR-BRIDGE-03 at 13x informative strata, H1 still not refuted, surviving cells 14->1) converge on the same negative finding, stable under a 13-fold power increase.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Preservation does not give Realization
b_rows_sample.statement: Hhat(Q|R5)=0 (adequate) is a separate fact from O(R5)=Q(D) (realized): a fixed decoder can fail on information-theoretically adequate data because it was fixed in advance and not refit; flagged as a design defect that the KR-REP-REDUCTION chain never operationalized this separation (no dropped record/source ever made constraint C fail), so 'the separation is real; that experiment could not exhibit it.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Eliminability does not give Realization
b_rows_sample.statement: Not derivable merely from the other two separations (explicitly not a corollary): Zero is defined via Pi, which is read-disjoint from Q by construction, so it carries no information about Q's recoverability 'by design' — verified rather than assumed.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Realization ⟹ Adequacy
b_rows_sample.statement: Standing conjecture that if a fixed decoder recovers Q from R on every observed case, R determines Q on the realized cases; refutable by a decoder that is right by luck (correct on every observed case while the fiber is Q-heterogeneous); explicitly 'not tested.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Do the separations survive a non-synthetic carrier?
b_rows_sample.statement: Flagged as the central transfer problem: whether eliminability/preservation/realization separations generalize beyond the tested synthetic carrier is explicitly open.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The estimand for any bridge claim is the within-stratum effect.
b_rows_sample.statement: The programme's central methodological error was estimating the wrong quantity competently — the marginal P(A|Z)-P(A|not Z) was already known to be confounded before KR-BRIDGE-02 ran; re-estimating it produced a false 'H2 SUPPORTED'; the correct estimand is the Mantel-Haenszel within-stratum effect.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A stratum is informative iff (a_k+b_k)>0 ∧ (c_k+d_k)>0 ∧ (a_k+c_k)>0 ∧ (b_k+d_k)>0
b_rows_sample.statement: Both Zero and non-Zero must occur and both Adequate and Inadequate must occur for a stratum to be informative; strata at deterministic extremes contribute nothing, explaining why flattening the redundancy distribution failed (balance is not power) and why choosing a finer stratification variable (multiplicity partition, then partition x |S|) gave 13x the informative strata.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Sign agreement alone is not replication.
b_rows_sample.statement: Under a sign-only replication rule, 14 cells 'replicated' with |RD|~0.001 and 12 of 14 had no stratum CI excluding zero; all 14 collapsed at higher power. Replication requires sign agreement AND clearing a substantive floor on both splits AND at least one stratum's 95% CI excluding zero; per-stratum RDs must be reported, not only the pooled MH estimate.

b_rows_sample.anchor: If the floor is declared after first inspection, record that fact in the artifact
b_rows_sample.statement: Effect-size floors must be declared and used as a reporting tier rather than a filter (publish every surviving cell at both tiers) since at n~10^5 statistical significance is not evidence of anything; a post-inspection floor must be disclosed as such.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Bootstrap CI on Ĥ ... [DEFECT] invalid here
b_rows_sample.statement: Estimator hygiene register: N_viol is exact and bias-free (authoritative for combinatorial adequacy questions), the Miller-Madow correction is used for Hhat, Haldane+0.5/Woolf CI is used for sparse odds-ratio tables, and bootstrap CI on Hhat is invalid because resampling duplicates cases and depresses conditional entropy.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Within the tested deduplication regime, redundancy behaves as a common cause of Zero occurrence and of inadequacy.
b_rows_sample.statement: Standard formalized here: never state a regime-specific empirical finding as a general causal law; a single-mechanism explanation of the KR-BRIDGE-01 confound was itself withdrawn once the Zero-count was found constant at r=1 but varying at r=2, showing the exact RD=0 had two different causes.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Power is a property of the informative region, not of n.
b_rows_sample.statement: Measured across four candidate power levers: population size (no effect, 73/74/70 across n=1500/4000/8000) and flattening the confounder distribution (73->75, no effect) both do nothing, while record count (73->233) and finer stratification variable (~30->388) are the effective levers; when power stops responding to sampling, the constraint has moved into the design (the 67 dead cells are invariant across nine generator regimes because the adequacy definition itself saturates).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Everything in this set is built from six objects and one operator.
b_rows_sample.statement: Theory 01 fixes the six-object signature of the KnowledgeOS transformation carrier: D (data, a finite multiset of records), T (transformation D->R), R=T(D) (representation), Q (inquiry D->Y), Pi (observable R->O), O (decoder R->Y), and C (constraint predicate on R), plus the inquiry frame Pi_frame=(Q,C,O) with O fixed in advance.

b_rows_sample.anchor: a record r = (value, source, tag, timestamp)
b_rows_sample.statement: A record in the tested carriers is r=(value,source,tag,timestamp), optionally a derived rank; explicitly flagged as an experimental carrier, not declared to be the mathematical carrier of KnowledgeOS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Set subtraction D \ S is INVALID wherever a field is relative.
b_rows_sample.statement: The elimination operator E_S must be typed to the level it acts at and must recompute relative fields (e.g. within-group rank) after removing S; naive set subtraction D\S leaves stale relative values and produces a representation the level's own rules forbid.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero is indexed by (T,Π) and by the subset S; adequacy by (T,Q) and the population; realization by (T,Q,O) and the case.
b_rows_sample.statement: Zero, Adequacy and Realization are defined with different index sets and are not three readings of one quantity: Zero_{T,Pi}(S;D) <=> Pi(T(D))=Pi(T(E_S(D))); Adequate(T,Q) <=> Hhat(Q|T(D))=0; Realized(T,Q,O) <=> O(T(D))=Q(D).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Π and Q must read disjoint fields, and disjointness must be discharged on the triple (Π, Q, T), not the pair (Π, Q).
b_rows_sample.statement: An anti-circularity requirement (candidate FR-003) is proposed: read-disjointness of Pi and Q must be verified on the triple (Pi,Q,T) because T can derive an output field Pi reads from sources Pi never declared; two concrete KR-BRIDGE-02 failures (a rank field secretly shared with Q's tag field, and an arity observable secretly reading value via deduplication survivorship) show declaration is not verification.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS has no declared mathematical carrier.
b_rows_sample.statement: Every experiment used a deliberately small numerical carrier (|D|<=6) so fibers would collide and adequacy would be measurable; this is a calibration choice, not an ontological one, and the move to documents/claims/entities/relations/provenance/contradictions/temporal states/evidence is the open research problem.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A transformation family is either sequential (Rk+1 = Tk(Rk)) or parallel (Rk = Tk(D)) — never silently mixed
b_rows_sample.statement: Sequential vs parallel transformation families is a permanent type-discipline rule, load-bearing because the data-processing inequality (document 04) applies to sequential families and not to parallel ones.

group_evidence.why_grouped: labels co-occur in the same contribution's labels[] 3 separate times across the corpus

a_rows_sample.anchor: Zoom lost determination in ~7% of cases and gained it in none. ... Refinement(K,Q) ⇏ Determination(K',Q) ... Refinement -> possible loss of determination. ... Representation != Knowledge != Determination.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reports the KR-ZOOM-01 finding that zoom (refinement) lost determination in ~7% of tested cases and gained it in 0%, giving Refinement(K,Q) ⇏ Determination(K',Q) and, in the tested regime, refinement can reduce rather than improve epistemic determination -- counterintuitive since more detail is normally expected to help; explicitly fits the existing Representation≠Knowledge≠Determination separation; flagged as a candidate [EXP] result, not yet a universal theorem.

b_rows_sample.anchor: If it simply removed dimensions, then the 7% result does not yet test your actual idea of zoom. ... Experimental Zoom != Your intended Inquiry Zoom. ... 'No dimension survives a zoom' is largely a consequence of the experimental implementation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reinterprets KR-ZOOM-01's ~7% determination-loss result and its 'no dimension survives a zoom' finding as consequences of the experiment implementing dimension-elimination (Anchor-restricted representation) rather than the intended inquiry-focused investigation, giving Experimental Zoom != intended Inquiry Zoom -- the 7% result should not yet be used as evidence against the intended KnowledgeOS Zoom concept, though it may remain a valid result about the specific operator actually tested.
