a_rows_sample.anchor: Proposition | A meaningful statement that can be true or false. | P=(Entity,Dimension,Value) ... Assertion | A proposition put forward as true, with a specific epistemic status... Knowledge | An assertion that satisfies the epistemic criteria for knowledge (justified true belief)
a_rows_sample.statement: Splits the Knowledge Atom into a three-level hierarchy Proposition subset-of Assertion subset-of Knowledge: Proposition=(E,D,V) is content without commitment; Assertion=(P,Sigma,Evidence,tau,Provenance) is a proposition put forward as true; Knowledge=(A,Justification,True) is a justified-true assertion; corrects the earlier Knowledge Atom to actually be an Assertion, not raw Knowledge.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Who determines True? KnowledgeOS observes, reconstructs, compares, challenges and guides. It generally cannot access Truth itself... Truth \neq Truth Assessment
a_rows_sample.statement: Rejects making absolute Truth an internal primitive of Knowledge, since KnowledgeOS cannot access Truth directly; replaces the three-level model with four levels (Proposition -> Assertion -> Epistemically Accepted -> Reality/Omega), where 'Knowledge' becomes K=(A,Justification,TruthAssessment) rather than requiring literal correspondence to reality.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Observation \rightarrow Candidate Proposition(s) ... because an observation can be ambiguous. ... 'Host responds on port 8081' -> P1/P2/P3
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects 'Observe -> Proposition' to 'Observation -> Candidate Proposition(s)', since one observation (e.g. a host responding on a port) can support multiple distinct, non-exclusive candidate propositions requiring Zero/Lord/Semantic-Reconstruction to disambiguate.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K_t = \mathcal{E}_t(\mathcal{A}_t) ... Knowledge isn't necessarily one object. It is a state of knowledge over many propositions and assertions.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reframes Knowledge from a single giant tuple to a Knowledge State K_t = E_t(A_t), an epistemic evaluation function over the set of currently available assertions A_t, foreshadowing K_{t+1}=Update(K_t,Observation_t,Zero_t,Lord_t,Evidence_t).

a_rows_sample.anchor: X_t \rightarrow O_t \rightarrow R_t \rightarrow A_t \rightarrow K_t
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the too-simple Reality->Observation->Knowledge pipeline into X_t (domain/reality) -> O_t (observation) -> R_t (semantic reconstruction/interpretation) -> A_t (assertion) -> K_t (knowledge state), with the critical point Observation ≠ Interpretation ≠ Assertion ≠ Knowledge, illustrated with the Bhīṣma example (seeing him = observation; 'Bhīṣma is a person' = interpretation; 'Bhīṣma is Arjuna's grandfather' = assertion; the same claim with provenance and epistemic qualification = knowledge).

a_rows_sample.anchor: P = \text{a semantically evaluable claim about entities, relationships, states or events}
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes Proposition as a semantically evaluable claim (examples: IsOnBattlefield(Bhishma), GrandfatherOf(Bhishma,Arjuna), OpponentOf(Bhishma,Arjuna)), distinguished from Assertion: Proposition ≠ Assertion, and Assertion = Proposition + Epistemic Qualification + Provenance. Flagged as a distinction that 'should be frozen'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A_3 = Inference( A_1,A_2,\ldots, Rule, Assumptions, Provenance )
a_rows_sample.statement: Extends Infer(A_1,A_2,Rule)->A_3 to require every derived assertion to carry Rule, Assumptions, and Provenance so KnowledgeOS can explain 'why do you believe this?': every derived assertion traceable to source assertions + inference rule + assumptions + context, called essential for deterministic assurance.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Document \neq Knowledge
a_rows_sample.statement: Rejects the naive Documents->Chunk->Embedding->VectorDB->RAG->LLM architecture as 'not KnowledgeOS' because it bypasses the epistemic model: a document is not knowledge but an information-bearing source from which observations/assertions may be constructed — Document ≠ Knowledge, Document ≠ Evidence — illustrated by Document->Observation->Candidate Assertion->Evidence->Knowledge State.

a_rows_sample.anchor: LLM\ Output \neq Knowledge
a_rows_sample.statement: Names three constitutional invariants for sources: (1) Source ≠ Knowledge (Document/API Response/Git Repository ≠ Knowledge); (2) LLM Output ≠ Knowledge — LLM Output -> Candidate Interpretation -> Epistemic Processing -> Knowledge; (3) Retrieval ≠ Knowledge Creation — Retrieve(Q) -> EvidenceCandidates -> Evaluate -> Knowledge. Overarching principle: 'Sources provide information; KnowledgeOS constructs governed knowledge from it. LLMs interpret; KnowledgeOS evaluates and governs. Retrieval supplies evidence candidates; it does not automatically create knowledge.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: Interpret: Observation \times Context \rightarrow CandidateMeaning
a_rows_sample.statement: Interpret:Observation×Context->CandidateMeaning is where the structural parser, semantic parser, domain model, and LLM participate, worked through 'those with whom I have to fight' -> structural parsing -> semantic parsing -> candidate semantic structure -> candidate dimensions {Actor,Target,Action,Relationship,Obligation,Context} — explicitly 'not yet accepted knowledge'. CandidateAssertion=(Proposition,Sources,Interpretation,Context), e.g. 'Bhīṣma is Arjuna's grandfather' becomes a candidate proposition via Interpret->CandidateAssertions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Assess: CandidateAssertion \times Evidence \times Rules \times Context \rightarrow EpistemicAssessment
a_rows_sample.statement: Assess:CandidateAssertion×Evidence×Rules×Context->EpistemicAssessment produces Σ_A=(Acquisition,Support,Uncertainty,Validity) per explicit policy, contrasting e.g. (Acquisition=Reported,Support=Moderate,Uncertainty=Moderate,Validity=Current) against (Acquisition=AI-Generated,Support=None,Uncertainty=High,Validity=Unknown) depending on what actually supports the proposition. CandidateAssertion --Assessment--> Assertion=(P,E,Σ,Π,τ,C,ID); K_{t+1}=δ(K_t,A). Full acquisition chain: X->Artifact->Observation->Interpretation->CandidateAssertion->Assessment->Assertion->K_{t+1}, stated to be 'already a computable architecture'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: \mathcal P = \mathcal P_F \cup \mathcal P_N \cup \mathcal P_Q \cup \mathcal P_H \cup \mathcal P_I \ldots
a_rows_sample.statement: After ten tests, provisionally establishes 'Source Observation is computationally realizable' across documents, DB results, internet resources, human statements, LLM outputs, code, rules, ADRs, constitutions and instructions, preserving Source event ≠ Meaning ≠ Assertion. Surfaces two explicit unresolved theoretical points without deciding them: Open Point A — whether one Proposition abstraction P_F∪P_N∪P_Q∪P_H∪P_I∪... (factual/normative/definitional/instructional/question/hypothesis/interpretation) with an explicit semantic type suffices, versus needing genuinely distinct object types; Open Point B — whether the Observation model should stay unified (with acquisition method/type recording measurement vs statement vs database vs LLM etc.) rather than creating separate Observation concepts per source class.

a_rows_sample.anchor: one Proposition abstraction, with explicit semantic type.
a_rows_sample.statement: Poses two explicit architectural-fork questions to the domain authority rather than deciding unilaterally: Question 1 — should factual/normative/definitional/instructional/hypothetical/interrogative content be different TYPES of semantic proposition under one common Proposition abstraction (recommended: Yes — one Proposition abstraction with explicit semantic type, rather than unrelated objects)? Question 2 — should the observation model stay unified, with acquisition method/type recording whether it came from measurement/database/document/human/LLM/API/parser (recommended: Yes)? If both are agreed, proposes formally closing Observation and moving to 'Computational Closure 2 — Interpretation', testing whether parsing+ontology+rules+LLM+human interpretation can transform arbitrary source observations into candidate semantic structures 'without pretending that interpretation is truth'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Should KnowledgeOS be allowed to create an Assertion with an explicitly unresolved epistemic state
a_rows_sample.statement: Poses and then answers the pivotal admission-boundary design choice: should an Assertion require passing a minimum admission threshold, or may it hold an explicitly unresolved epistemic state (Unknown/Hypothesized/WeaklySupported)? Recommends and then (in a 'Domain Authority' voice) DECIDES the latter: Assertion ≠ Proven Truth. Rationale given for rejecting the threshold alternative: it would remove Zero's ability to detect gaps (no representation for Unknown/Hypothesized), remove Lord's ability to generate candidates (no place for them to reside), sever the Observation->Interpretation->Candidate->Assertion provenance chain, damage auditability (no record of 'what we considered but did not accept'), make the incomplete-question problem unsolvable, collapse the Unknown-vs-Absent distinction, and break the learning trajectory Hypothesized->WeaklySupported->StronglySupported.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Truth = "This is what we currently represent, with this degree of support, uncertainty, and validity."
a_rows_sample.statement: Re-runs all eight test cases (DB result -> StronglySupported; unstructured document -> WeaklySupported; internet page -> WeaklySupported with caveats; human statement -> Reported; LLM output -> Hypothesized; incomplete question -> no assertion created, Zero detects gap, clarification requested; conflicting sources -> both assertions remain in the Knowledge State with a detected Conflict; unknown value -> Assertion(Unknown)) through the new admission model. States the redefined meaning of 'the single source of truth': Truth = 'this is what we currently represent, with this degree of support, uncertainty, and validity', NOT 'this is factually correct in reality' — the formalization of Knowledge ≠ Reality. Six constitutional invariants listed: Assertion≠Proven Truth; admission does not require verification; Unknown is a valid epistemic state (not absence of an assertion); epistemic status can evolve; multiple epistemic states can coexist (Conflicting is valid); provenance is preserved. Declares the Epistemic Admission Boundary computationally closed and proceeds to 'Computational Closure 3 — The Knowledge State'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A \not\equiv Truth(P)
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes Assertion A=(P,E,Σ,Π,τ,C,ID) with A≢Truth(P): A is 'KnowledgeOS's governed representation of P'. Two assertions of the identical proposition 'Nexus.version=3.69' can carry different epistemic states (Σ_A=(Observed,Strong,Low,Current) vs Σ_B=(Reported,Weak,High,Unknown)) and are 'not epistemically equivalent', giving Assertion⇏StrongEvidence, Assertion⇏Certainty, Assertion⇏Truth.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Admit(P,\Pi_1) \neq Admit(P,\Pi_2)
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces admission policy Π_adm with Admit(P_c,E,C,Π_adm)->{Assertion|Reject|Defer|RequestMoreEvidence}; admission is purpose-dependent, Admit(P,Π_1)≠Admit(P,Π_2) (an exploration policy may allow Weak support, a production-migration policy may require Strong support) — connecting directly to the Ideal State theory: an assertion can exist with Σ_K=Weak while the Ideal State requires Σ_I=Strong, producing a discrepancy rather than an invalid assertion. Distinguishes Admission ('may this proposition exist as governed knowledge?', Candidate->Assertion) from Validation ('does this assertion satisfy a particular requirement?', Assertion×Constraint->ValidationResult): Admission ≠ Validation — an assertion can be admitted (e.g. during discovery) yet later FAIL a validation (e.g. a migration requiring verified version) WITHOUT being deleted; it 'remains useful historical knowledge'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Assertion \in KnowledgeState ... KnowledgeState \neq SetOfAssertions
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects an earlier equation Assertion=Knowledge (too strong) to Assertion∈KnowledgeState while KnowledgeState≠SetOfAssertions: the Knowledge State is a structured object K_t=(Assertions,Evidence,Relationships,Conflicts,Gaps,Provenance,Context,History,Constraints), 'a structured state, not simply a bag of claims' — called 'an important DDD correction'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: \text{Evidence is not a property of a document.}
a_rows_sample.statement: Central correction: Evidence is not a property of a document but 'a relationship between an observation and a proposition under a context and an evaluation rule' — Evidence(O,P,C,R). Prevents the mistake 'the document says X, therefore X is evidence [for whatever P]'. Gives Evidence≠Observation, Evidence≠Source, Evidence≠Support, Evidence≠Truth as four fundamental distinctions, and shows the SAME observation can be evidence for one proposition and not another (Evidence(O,P_1)≠Evidence(O,P_2)) — 'evidence is therefore relational'. E=(O,P,R,C,T,Q,Π): observation, target proposition, evaluation rule, context, temporal applicability, quality assessment, provenance.

type_signature.domain: observation x proposition x context x rule

a_rows_sample.anchor: Conclusion = Inference(Premises,Rule,Context)
a_rows_sample.statement: Rejects 'the evidence voted for 3.69' informal aggregation, requiring Conclusion=Inference(Premises,Rule,Context) via an explicit inference rule (worked example: APIResponse.version=3.69 plus rule 'APIResponse(source=NexusProduction)=>CurrentVersion(NexusProduction)' yields the conclusion). Distinguishes four conclusion kinds: Deductive (Γ⊨P, entailed), Inductive (evidence increases support for a generalization without entailing it), Abductive (select the best explanation among hypotheses {H_1,...,H_n} — 'extremely relevant to KnowledgeOS'), Computational/derived (e.g. a version-vs-required-version comparison rule). Formalizes Conclusion object C_n=(P,Γ,R,κ,Σ,Π,t) (proposition, premises/evidence, inference rule, inference method, epistemic assessment, provenance, derivation time), letting KnowledgeOS answer 'why did you reach this conclusion?' not just 'what did you conclude?'.

b_rows_sample.anchor:
=> Of 10 propositions the corpus itself requires, 2 are cleanly expressible.
     THREE are inexpressible
b_rows_sample.statement: EXP-19: tested against 10 propositions the corpus itself states it needs to express, P=(Entity,Dimension,Value) cleanly expresses only 2; 3 are inexpressible (negation — no negative values in V_D; conditional — 'IF v>=3.60 THEN patch-current', the founding conditional-determination problem; universal quantification — 'every committee has >=3 members'); 2 are lossy (a validity interval collapses to one timestamp t; a unit is dropped); 1 ('A1 contradicts A2') is not a proposition at all in this type system and must be expressed as an R-edge instead, giving the theory two uncoordinated mechanisms for propositional content; 1 ('Nexus is ready to migrate') is expressible but empty, holding the conclusion with no way to express the rule that produced it; 1 ('Nexus.version is UNKNOWN') is ambiguous between a value-space category error and true absence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ### 2.1 `P = (E,D,V)` — **the corpus refutes it in the same file that supplies it**
b_rows_sample.statement: Divergence 1: Q14 (20260826-182409) supplies P=(E,D,V) and then, in its own §3 titled 'The biggest mathematical problem: Proposition = Entity + Dimension + Value', calls it too restrictive and recommends P=(S,ρ,O,Γ) as 'a very important correction' — never adopted (AttributeProposition occurs in exactly one file); Step 262 reopens it and records it as an open sub-test.

b_rows_sample.anchor: | 6 | Can evidence exist without an assertion? | 🟡 **type-yes, semantically-no** |
b_rows_sample.statement: The sharpest of nine mandated counterexamples: E_q is indexed by the claim q it is evidence for (Step 230.15), but the theory's amended 9-field evidence record drops this index, making evidence free-floating; this loses both the ability to say what an item is evidence for, and the domain the independence relation (needed for corroboration) would need to live on.

group_evidence.why_grouped: labels share the notation 'P=(E,D,V)'

a_rows_sample.anchor: R[W] reducing a query about a later situation to a query about the initial situation ... Eval_c \neq ReasoningAlgorithm ... Reason_S(K,r) \rightarrow EvidenceForEvaluation rather than claiming Regression = Eval
a_rows_sample.statement: Regression R[W] is offered as a candidate reasoning mechanism feeding Eval_c, explicitly distinguished as Eval_c != ReasoningAlgorithm: Reason_S(K,r) -> EvidenceForEvaluation, rejecting the identification Regression = Eval.

a_rows_sample.anchor: progression can be significantly more computationally difficult ... BackwardReasoning \neq ForwardSimulation ... Regress(K,r) and Progress(K,e) with no assumption that one is universally superior ... query answering may favor regression; state evolution naturally uses progression; planning may require both
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces two candidate reasoning mechanisms Regress(K,r) and Progress(K,e) with no universal superiority assumed (BackwardReasoning != ForwardSimulation), noting progression's typically higher computational cost, and use-case guidance (query answering favors regression, state evolution favors progression, planning may require both).

a_rows_sample.anchor: DK.1 State and History [DERIVED] ... DK.3 Successor-State Semantics [PROP — EXPERIMENT REQUIRED] ... DK.5 Executable History [PROP] ... DK.6 Transition Composition [DERIVED], semantics of choice and iteration remain [OPEN] ... DK.8 Epistemic Update [PROP] ... DK.9 Temporal and Concurrent Transitions [PROP — REQUIRES TIME/FRAME DECISION]
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a 9-section 'KNOWLEDGEOS — DYNAMIC KNOWLEDGE AND TRANSITION SEMANTICS' research-draft addition (DK.1 State/History [DERIVED], DK.2 Transition Applicability [DERIVED], DK.3 Successor-State Semantics [PROP-EXPERIMENT REQUIRED], DK.4 Boundary/Persistence [DERIVED+PROP], DK.5 Executable History [PROP], DK.6 Transition Composition [DERIVED, choice/iteration OPEN], DK.7 Reasoning Over Transitions [DERIVED], DK.8 Epistemic Update [PROP], DK.9 Temporal/Concurrent Transitions [PROP-REQUIRES TIME/FRAME DECISION]), explicitly not yet called Theory v1.3, with per-section status tags distinct from the KR.1-KR.10 DL-thread tags in S2523/S2524.

a_rows_sample.anchor: R[F(x,do(a,s))] = R[Phi_F(x,a,s)] ... The Regression Theorem: D \models W \iff D_{S_0}\cup D_{una}\models R[W] ... Progression is harder than regression—it may not be first-order definable.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the formal Regression Theorem (D |= W iff D_S0 ∪ D_una |= R[W], reducing entailment over the full domain axiomatization to entailment over the initial-situation axioms plus unique-names axioms via regression R), and notes progression may not be first-order definable, making it strictly harder than regression -- both retained as [DERIVED] legitimate reasoning mechanisms.

a_rows_sample.anchor: "claim": "regression and progression answer the same queries", ... "n_checks": 12, "all_agree": true
a_rows_sample.statement: Executed equivalence check: for 6 action sequences (including empty, single, and multi-fluent-affecting sequences) crossed with 2 fluents, backward regression and forward progression agree on all 12 resulting truth values, confirming the regression theorem holds in this toy basic action theory.

a_rows_sample.anchor: class Situation: """A situation IS a history: a finite sequence of actions.  NOT a state.""" ... def successor(self, a, state): """Successor state axiom:  F' = gamma+ ∨ (F ∧ ¬gamma-)""" ... def regress(self, fluent, sit): """REGRESSION: rewrite a query about sit into a query about S0, by unwinding the successor-state axiom backwards."""
a_rows_sample.statement: A minimal but faithful executable model of Reiter's situation calculus: a Situation as an immutable action tuple (explicitly a history, not a state), an ActionTheory with Poss/successor(SSA)/progress/executable/regress methods, used to generate all five A1-A5 experimental results in this batch; module docstring explicitly frames these as verification tests of Reiter's machinery, not a KnowledgeOS implementation, and states nothing here promotes any Reiter concept to a KnowledgeOS primitive.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Regression and progression agree on 12/12 checks across 6 action sequences x 2 fluents (A3). Executed, not asserted. ... Progression computes A_{t+1} and discards the history. KR-HISTORY established that the kernel writes history (and reads it 0 times). Progression satisfies the read behaviour and not the write obligation. ... progression for the state, history retained for audit, regression as the mechanism that makes retention useful rather than merely dutiful.
a_rows_sample.statement: New synthesis: regression and progression serve complementary, not competing, roles for KnowledgeOS -- progression advances the state (satisfying the kernel's 0-read behavior) while history must still be retained to satisfy a separate write obligation established by KR-HISTORY, and regression is what makes that retained history useful for audit/verification rather than merely dutiful storage; P10 (progression sufficient alone) is refuted on exactly this basis. The regression theorem's formal guarantee is unavailable to KnowledgeOS (no basic action theory exists yet) -- only the mechanism's shape transfers.

a_rows_sample.anchor: IC-2 Regression as a verification mechanism | Corpus basis: KR-HISTORY: history is written and never read -- regression is what would make it readable for audit ... Current evidence: A3: agrees with progression 12/12 ... Missing evidence: KnowledgeOS has no basic action theory, so the theorem's guarantee is unavailable -- only the mechanism's shape ... Maturity/Status: SUPPORTED -- the most transferable item, and still not adoptable
a_rows_sample.statement: IC-2: regression (R[phi] unwinding the successor-state axioms to S0) is proposed as a verification mechanism, motivated by the corpus finding (KR-HISTORY) that history is written and never read -- regression is what would make it readable for audit. Terminates on regressable queries, deterministic, and A3 confirms regression agrees with progression 12/12. But KnowledgeOS has no basic action theory, so the regression theorem's formal guarantee is unavailable -- only the mechanism's shape transfers. Status: SUPPORTED as the most transferable item, yet still not adoptable.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K_{t+1}=Succ(K_t,e_t)
b_rows_sample.statement: Instead of treating delta as an unspecified transformer, investigate K_{t+1}=Succ(K_t,e_t) where each state component carries conditions for becoming true, becoming false, and persistence — i.e. the frame problem, borrowed from situation-calculus successor-state axioms F(x,do(a,s)) ≡ gamma_F(x,a,s) v (F(x,s) & ¬delta_F(x,a,s)).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Table: what I would actually add to KnowledgeOS Theory v1.3 (T1-T5) vs What I would NOT adopt
b_rows_sample.statement: Recorded editorial recommendation: five candidate theoretical commitments (T1 explicit/implicit knowledge, T2 reasoning is semantics-dependent Cn_S(K), T3 evaluation may consume implicit knowledge Eval_c(Cn_S(K),r,Gamma), T4 state transition needs persistence semantics Succ_S, T5 explanation is not determination) proposed for Theory v1.3 as strong candidates, none yet kernel-promoted; explicitly rejects Sat=FOL-entailment, Zero=CWA, Zero=Delta=empty universally, Boundary=frame axioms, delta=situation calculus, Identity=unique-names+domain-closure, DL=Boundary-taxonomy, mandatory default reasoning, FOL-as-representation-language, and YES/NO/UNKNOWN-sufficiency.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K_{t+1}=Succ_{\mathcal S}(K_t,e_t) ... successor semantics must account for: newly introduced content; removed or invalidated content; persistent content; contextual applicability; provenance/history. This does not define δ as situation calculus.
b_rows_sample.statement: delta(K_t,e_t)->K_{t+1} remains an open transition problem; adopts K_{t+1}=Succ_S(K_t,e_t) as a research framework requiring successor semantics to account for five things: newly introduced content, removed/invalidated content, persistent content, contextual applicability, and provenance/history. Explicitly: this defines situation-calculus successor-state reasoning as a formal candidate to investigate delta against, not a definition of delta itself.

b_rows_sample.anchor: What This Book Confirms: R_req=TBox, Sat(K_t,r)=Instance checking, Contradiction=Concept inconsistency detection, Boundary=Frame axioms, Taxonomy=Classification hierarchy, Specialized reasoning=Tableau/structural subsumption, Nonmonotonicity=Default reasoning extension, Uncertainty=Probabilistic/fuzzy extensions, Composition=Role/concept composition, delta=Successor state axioms
b_rows_sample.statement: Consolidated 'what this book confirms' mapping table asserting the handbook validates a large set of unqualified KnowledgeOS identifications: R_req=TBox, Sat(K_t,r)=Instance checking, Contradiction=Concept inconsistency, Boundary=Frame axioms, Taxonomy=Classification hierarchy, Specialized reasoning=Tableau algorithms/structural subsumption, Incremental knowledge=ABox assertions, Explanation=Subsumption explanation, Nonmonotonicity=Default reasoning, Uncertainty=Probabilistic/fuzzy extensions, Composition=Role/concept composition, delta=Successor state axioms.

b_rows_sample.statement: Refines the successor-state candidate: rather than starting from delta:K x E -> K, first ask which state predicates change/persist/are invalidated, giving K_{t+1} = Added ∪ Persisted ∪ Reclassified ∪ Removed as a rigorous (not yet definitional) research framework for delta.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KR.1 Representation Layers ... KR.6 Open-World Constraint ... KR.9 Transition ... KR.10 Expressiveness and Tractability
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes inserting a 10-section 'KNOWLEDGE REPRESENTATION AND STRUCTURED REASONING' theory addition (KR.1 Representation Layers, KR.2 Reasoning Cn_S, KR.3 Subsumption, KR.4 Classification, KR.5 Consistency, KR.6 Open-World Constraint, KR.7 Evaluation via reasoning-service family, KR.8 Explanation/Missing Assumptions, KR.9 Transition/successor-state with Boundary!=FrameAxiom retained, KR.10 Expressiveness/Tractability), consolidating all the file's individually-derived candidates into one proposed section.

b_rows_sample.anchor: F(do(a,s)) \equiv \gamma_F^+(a,s) \lor (F(s)\land\neg\gamma_F^-(a,s)) ... X_{t+1}=Add_X(e_t,K_t)\lor(X_t\land\neg Remove_X(e_t,K_t)) ... K_{t+1}=Apply(K_t,e_t,Add(e_t),Remove(e_t),Persist(e_t))

a_rows_sample.anchor: Six-Phase Methodology: Samshaya, Pramana, Pancha Avayava, Tarka, Hetvabhasa, Nirnaya
a_rows_sample.statement: Maps the six-phase AI-implementation methodology to KnowledgeOS parallels: doubt analysis -> evidence sourcing -> structured reasoning -> contradiction detection -> fallacy detection -> decision/knowledge state.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 1. Generating valid cognition (prama) -> 2. Initiating inquiry through structured doubt (samsaya) -> 3. Constructing and evaluating theory (siddhanta, avayava, nirnaya) -> 4. Testing conclusions through formalised discourse (vada, jalpa, vitanda) -> [back to 1]
a_rows_sample.statement: Describes Nyaya Sutra's iterative four-phase cognitive cycle (valid cognition -> structured doubt -> theory construction/evaluation -> formalised discourse testing -> repeat), offered as a lifecycle model complementing KnowledgeOS's created->validated->approved->active->deprecated states.

a_rows_sample.statement: Maps the 16 padarthas onto KnowledgeOS concepts and argues knowledge evolution should be represented as Observation->Doubt->Investigation->Reasoning->Challenge->Determination->Knowledge State rather than a simple Created->Approved->Published pipeline; proposes H-KOS-Lifecycle-Reasoning-001.

a_rows_sample.statement: States the core extraction of the reviewed paper: KnowledgeOS needs a formal discipline governing how claims move from uncertainty to justified conclusion, citing Nyaya's emphasis on critical analysis (purvapaksa), argument rigor, and siddhanta (conclusion).

a_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS needs a reasoning lifecycle, not only a knowledge lifecycle... a_rows_sample.statement: Restates the 16-padartha mapping and proposes INV-KOS-ReasoningLifecycle-001 requiring preservation of the complete epistemic path from uncertainty to justified conclusion.

a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces a 'Cognitive Review Mode' design principle: not every belief undergoes full verification; a default-trust mode operates until reasonable doubt triggers escalation into knowledge-source-plus-tarka investigation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge Confidence State Machine: OBSERVED -> INFERRED -> ACCEPTED -> CHALLENGED -> UNDER REVIEW -> VALIDATED / REJECTED. Not every fact needs an expensive review.

a_rows_sample.statement: Drafts ADR-KOS-EPI-004 restricting deep verification workflows to being triggered by contradiction, uncertainty, or challenge (not applied universally).

a_rows_sample.anchor: > **Corroboration C-3:** **doubt ≠ contradiction**, from an independent tradition... This study therefore does NOT introduce a second `saṃśaya` candidate.** It **extends the existing one**
a_rows_sample.statement: Corroboration C-3: the Gita treats saṃśaya (doubt, cut by instruction) and viṣāda (contradiction/paralysis, not removed by instruction alone) as two distinct pathologies with two distinct remedies -- corroborating Contr≠Unknown. Per ES-005.4 discipline, this explicitly extends (rather than duplicates) the corpus's existing samsaya-structured-doubt-state candidate (from a prior Nyaya extraction) with a new contrast the Nyaya source lacked: samsaya initiates inquiry, visada halts it -- same family, opposite dynamics.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero = Neutral starting condition ... It begins as: UNKNOWN
b_rows_sample.statement: Zero as neutral knowledge state: Zero != Nothing, it is a neutral starting condition. A new knowledge object begins without authority, evidence, validation or interpretation -- it begins as UNKNOWN.

b_rows_sample.anchor: UNKNOWN != False. UNKNOWN != Missing. UNKNOWN = Known unresolved state
b_rows_sample.statement: UNKNOWN is proposed as a first-class state, distinct from False and from Missing: UNKNOWN = a known, unresolved state.

b_rows_sample.anchor: UNKNOWN != False. UNKNOWN != Missing. UNKNOWN = Known unresolved state
b_rows_sample.statement: Zero lens: UNKNOWN restated as a first-class known-unresolved state, distinct from False and Missing.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS should not force: Unknown -> False / Unknown -> Guess / Unknown -> Empty. Instead: Unknown -> Known Unknown
b_rows_sample.statement: Combining Zero ('unknown is a valid state') with ECS ('failure does not destroy truth, failure pauses advancement'): Unknown should be preserved and later resolved, never forced into False/Guess/Empty.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Different observations may represent different projections of the same underlying object.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reinterprets the elephant-and-blind-men story (cited by the source) not as 'everyone is equally right' but as 'different observations may represent different projections of the same underlying object', formalized as perspectives A/B/C/D undergoing structural comparison to yield a common invariant = ZERO.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge is perspective dependent, but structure may be perspective invariant.
b_rows_sample.statement: Abstracts the source's citation of Subhash Kak's six-darsanas-as-cube-walls metaphor into the principle 'knowledge is perspective dependent, but structure may be perspective invariant', with the research question 'what survives when we rotate the perspective?' answered by ZERO = invariant.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Z_M(K) = invariant across plausible worlds ... The technology disappears. The invariant remains.
b_rows_sample.statement: Introduces modal Zero Z_M(K) = invariant across plausible worlds, alongside a claimed prior representation Zero Z_R(K)=invariant across representations and temporal Zero Z_T(K)=invariant across time; illustrated by four possible event-bus technology choices (Kafka/RabbitMQ/sync API/another event bus) all preserving the invariant requirement 'evidence publication must remain replayable' -- the technology disappears, the invariant remains.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Z = ⋂_i Structure(I_i) ... What structure remains invariant across competing models, representations, times, and perspectives? That may be one of our strongest candidates for robust knowledge.
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes the Zero lens as Z=intersection_i Structure(I_i) over interpretations generated from multiple world models W1..Wn (not necessarily literal set intersection in implementation), asking what structure remains invariant across competing models, representations, times and perspectives, proposed as one of the strongest candidates for robust knowledge.

b_rows_sample.anchor: O_i = π_i(R) ... O1 ≠ O2 doesn't necessarily mean R1 ≠ R2. It may simply mean π1 ≠ π2. This gives us a very useful projection lens.
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes the elephant analogy as a projection: observation Oi=pi_i(R) for underlying reality/object R and observer perspective pi_i, concluding that differing observations O1!=O2 need not imply differing underlying realities R1!=R2 -- it may simply reflect differing perspectives pi1!=pi2 -- named the 'projection lens'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Z = Invariant(O1,...,On) ... Zero is not "nothing." It is the minimum invariant structure that survives changes in representation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Given observations O1..On, defines Z=Invariant(O1,...,On) and explicitly corrects a possible misreading: Zero is not 'nothing', it is the minimum invariant structure that survives changes in representation -- called one of the strongest concepts in the entire exploration.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Dhātu = transformation structure ... Zero = invariant structure ... what changed? / what remained?
b_rows_sample.statement: States a Dhatu/Zero duality: given O1 --T1--> O2 --T2--> O3, Dhatu asks what transformation generated the new state (Dhatu = transformation structure) while Zero asks what remained (Zero = invariant structure).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge itself should not be reduced to its representations.
b_rows_sample.statement: Zero-Lens result on Williamson: after removing beliefs, documents, language, databases, probabilities, possible worlds, embeddings, topics, LLMs, what survives is minimal: 'A participant is related to a proposition/content in a world/context/time such that the proposition is true and the participant is in a factive state of knowing.' Knowledge itself should not be reduced to its representations.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 1. Participants make commitments. 2. Commitments have inferential consequences. 3. Some commitments are supported/entitled...
b_rows_sample.statement: Zero-Lens extraction on Brandom (removing language/English/sentences/speech/Frege/Wittgenstein/philosophy) yields ten survivor claims: participants make commitments; commitments have inferential consequences; some commitments are supported/entitled; commitments can conflict; participants assess one another's commitments; new actions alter the state; implicit relations can become explicit; concepts are characterized partly by inferential roles; objectivity can emerge within social assessment; a claim is not merely a string but a position in a normative/inferential structure.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Unknown is not simply an error state. It is a legitimate epistemic condition.
b_rows_sample.statement: ASP answer-set semantics give TRUE/FALSE/UNKNOWN query results and ground at least three distinct kinds of 'unknown': unknown because alternatives remain (P and ¬P both possible), unknown because the agent is unaware (neither represented), and unknown because a default was blocked (an exception/missing condition prevented an otherwise-applicable default). The earlier flat UNKNOWN category should become an Epistemic Status taxonomy: true/false/unresolved-alternatives/not-represented-unaware/defeasibly-inferable-but-blocked/etc; the exact taxonomy remains a research question but the distinction itself is now strongly grounded.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Absence must not silently become an epistemic state.
b_rows_sample.statement: Danger flagged in the Projection model: 'If Projection P2 doesn't contain X, therefore X is false' would be wrong, since absence from a projection could mean not relevant, not visible, not assessed, outside scope, unavailable, superseded, or genuinely no longer justified — these are different meanings. This connects to the ZERO lens: absence must not silently become an epistemic state, giving another reason to preserve ZERO discipline within the Projection idea.

b_rows_sample.anchor: U(e) ∈ {alternative, unrepresented, blocked-default, outside-scope, computationally-unresolved}
b_rows_sample.statement: Unknownness U(e) is proposed not as a Boolean but a classification (alternative / unrepresented / blocked-default / outside-scope / computationally-unresolved), with the exact taxonomy left empirical and countable for future statistical analysis.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 1. There is an underlying world/domain. 2. A participant has beliefs/knowledge about it. 3. Only part of that knowledge may be explicitly represented...
b_rows_sample.statement: Zero-Lens extraction on Brachman & Levesque (removing FOL/Prolog/frames/description logic/SAT/default logic/Bayesian networks/STRIPS/GOLOG) yields twelve survivor claims: an underlying world/domain exists; a participant has beliefs/knowledge about it; only part is explicitly represented; representation is a mapping between domains; reasoning derives implicit content from explicit content; meaning depends on interpretation/context; different representation languages have different expressive power; reasoning capability is resource-limited; knowledge changes and can be revised; uncertainty/vagueness require richer representations; the same knowledge may have different representations; action depends on knowledge — described as extraordinarily close to the current model.

b_rows_sample.anchor: what survives across *both* phases is: **a knower/participant · something known · a ground · and a record that the two were connected.**
b_rows_sample.statement: Zero-Lens applied across both phases: after stripping optional attributes, what survives universally is a knower/participant, something known, a ground, and a record that the two were connected — every phase and nearly every model retains those four; nothing else survives universally. The corpus distinguishes 'nothing exists' from 'we do not know' (0258: 'Knowledge is not only about what exists'; formal law §9: unknown≠absent≠false). Whether UNKNOWN is the absence of Knowledge or a state of an identified object is NOT resolved by the corpus: formal law (⟨Z-1⟩) says UNKNOWN/ABSENT/FALSE/REJECTED are states of an identified epistemic object, while kernel document 125708 §17 pushes the other way ('UNKNOWN must not be a single epistemic state', eight readings) — no new state proposed here.

b_rows_sample.anchor: AF-004 · Zero's chronology inverts CF-005's apparent ordering
b_rows_sample.statement: The repository's 'third sense' of Zero (Z-KOS-001 meta-principle) and the absence-lens sense are BOTH dated 2026-08-22; the goal-gap function sense is the LATEST (2026-08-27 era) — inverting an apparent ordering implied by CF-005.

b_rows_sample.anchor: CF-005 · Zero naming collision — a third sense
b_rows_sample.statement: Repository Zero (Z-KOS-001) is a foundational meta-principle explicitly refused as kernel article and implementation object ('Zero is the name for that prevention', 'Zero != Component = Property of the boundaries'), whereas v0.2 Zero is the computable goal-gap function Zero(K, EC); same term, incompatible senses, extending the CON-01 lineage with an implementation-side third sense; no repository counterpart of the goal-gap function exists, and the eta-totality/G-residual question (T-9) stays open.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #1 — Knowledge as a generic object: forbidden in 208, used as an Owner in 210
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 208 Section 208.28 boxes a prohibition: the Data->Information->Evidence->Assessment->KnowledgeClaim transformations of semantic status 'should not [be collapsed] into one generic object called Knowledge.' Step 210 Section 210.25's matrix row I11 nonetheless assigns Owner='Knowledge' (and row I3 compounds it with 'Knowledge infrastructure'), the exact generic object Step 208 boxed a prohibition against two files earlier in the same band. Severity HIGH; neither Step-206 bounded context, and neither file notices.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #2 — Provenance composition (208) excludes the authority Step 209 requires
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 208 Section 208.25 asserts as an equality P(G)=P(A)∪P(E), boxed as 'provenance must be closed under semantic transformation.' Step 209 Section 209.4 requires Final(D)⇒DecisionBasis(D)∧Authority(D). Since Authority(D), the governance grant that made a decision final, is in neither P(A) nor P(E), a governed decision's provenance under Section 208.25 cannot contain its own authority, yet Step 209's own traceability requirement (Basis(D) including authority) demands that it does -- the two cannot both hold. Independently checked, the equality is additionally vacuous if closure holds (P(A)⊇P(E) implies the union is just P(A)) and self-refuting if it does not. Severity HIGH.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #3 — The evidence-strength scale is recalibrated between Step 210 and Step 212
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 210 Section 210.30 defines E_1=documentation, E_2=manual inspection, E_3=automated test, E_4=property-based test, E_5=formal verification. Step 212 Section 212.6 defines E_0=No evidence, E_1=Claim/documentation, E_2=Static implementation evidence, E_3=Executable test evidence, E_4=Runtime/production evidence, E_5=Formal verification. E_2, E_3 and E_4 disagree between the two files (only E_5 agrees), so a claim 'has E_4 evidence' means a property-based test under Step 210 and production observation under Step 212 -- entirely different assurance. Aggravating factor: Step 212's calibration silently matches the uncited Step 109's (E2=implementation, E4=runtime), so Step 212 restores an earlier convention without knowing it. Severity HIGH.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #4 — E_1 bound twice inside Step 210 itself
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 210 Section 210.20 writes E_1⇒P and E_2⇒¬P (evidence items entailing propositions); Step 210 Section 210.30, ten sections later, writes E_1=documentation (an ordinal assurance rung). Same symbol, same document, incompatible types, undisambiguated. Severity MEDIUM-HIGH.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #5 — Evidence/Test ordering reversed between Step 210's own boxed conclusion and Step 211's boxed conclusion
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 210 Section 210.40 boxes Invariant->Owner->Enforcement->Evidence->Test->Assurance; Step 211 Section 211.2 boxes I->Owner->Mechanism->Test->Evidence -- directly conflicting orderings, both boxed as conclusions in consecutive files. Step 210's own Section 210.1 tuple and Step 209's tail agenda both side with Step 211's ordering, so Step 210's boxed conclusion contradicts Step 210's own boxed tuple. Severity MEDIUM; the direction matters since Evidence->Test means evidence licenses the test while Test->Evidence means the test produces the evidence, which is what Steps 212-214 assume throughout.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #6 — min over assurance vs. the prohibition on scalarization, both boxed in Step 211
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 211 Section 211.6 states Assurance(I_global)<=min{Assurance(I_1),Assurance(I_2),...}; Step 211 Section 211.17 boxes 'Vector assurance is preferable to premature scalarization.' min over a set requires a total order on the codomain, but Section 211.9 makes assurance a 6-vector (only partially ordered), so evaluating min requires exactly the scalarization Section 211.17 forbids -- the two boxed positions of one file are mutually exclusive. Aggravated by Section 211.4's ordinal-only assurance-adjacent quantities and by Section 211.17's own use of cardinal values A_s=1, A_p=0, 0.83. Severity HIGH.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #7 — Step 212 builds ownership diagnostics and deletes the ownership data needed to run them
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 212 Section 212.15 boxes 'Ownerless Invariants' as a finding to explicitly search for (I exists but Owner(I)=empty set), yet Step 212 Section 212.4's register reprints all fifteen invariants with the Owner column removed (columns reduced to ID|Property|Target), and no search for ownerless invariants is performed anywhere in the file. Step 210's deleted Owner column contained exactly the data Sections 212.15/212.16 are designed to interrogate: 7 of 15 rows owned by a layer or pattern (effectively ownerless), 5 of 15 slash-shared. Severity HIGH.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #8 — F/D/P/U mandated in Step 213, applied zero times across Steps 213-215
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 213 Section 213.26 mandates that every important statement during reconstruction carry an [F]/[D]/[P]/[U] label ('our editorial control system'). A machine count of applied labels in Steps 213, 214, and 215 finds 4, 0, 0 respectively, and all four occurrences in 213 are the legend itself. Zero of the hundreds of statements in the three files that mandate the labels carry one, even though Section 213.26 explicitly scopes the requirement to these reconstruction documents themselves. Severity HIGH; this is a performative contradiction.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #9 — Step 214's self-assessment table violates Step 214's own boxed evidentiary rule eight lines later
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 214 Section 214.32 boxes 'no architectural claim should be stronger than the evidence supporting it.' Step 214 Section 214.33's final row states 'Risk of overclaiming | Explicitly controlled' -- a claim about the corpus's own overclaiming risk with zero supporting evidence, in a table that also self-awards 'Very strong' on five dimensions in a file containing no evidence at all. Severity MEDIUM-HIGH.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #10 — Three incompatible ledger arities inside Step 214
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 214 Section 214.1 boxes a 10-tuple EL_i=(Step,Artifact,Observation,Fact,Derivation,Decision,Architecture,Invariant,Evidence,Status); Section 214.6 gives a 15-field schema table; the Section 214 tail (line 1095) gives an 8-column matrix header whose columns barely overlap the 10-tuple's. Three incompatible schemas for 'the Evidence Ledger' in one file, with no reconciliation and no statement of which is normative. Severity MEDIUM.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #11 — Step 215 prohibits new formulas and mints three (four) in the same file
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 215 Section 215.30 prohibits 'creat[ing] more theoretical formulas merely because we can,' yet the same file mints R(S_i)=(O_i,L_i,A_i,V_i,U_i) (215.1), Convergence(I)=NumberOfIndependentEvidencePaths(I) (215.7), the boxed SemanticIntegrity∝DistinctionPreservation (215.10), and the boxed B=Synthesize(Evidence,Experiments,Failures,Insights,Architecture,PhilosophicalReflection) (215.32) -- four new formal objects, none computed. Severity MEDIUM; aggravated because the proportionality is not merely new but ill-typed, and Synthesize is never specified.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #12 — Step 215 exempts itself and its seven predecessors from its own discipline
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 215 Section 215.31 (Phase 1) targets S_1...S_182 -> EvidenceLedger, goal 'understand what actually happened'; the same file's closing paragraph defers 'what we previously called Step 183 onward' to a later decision about renaming or absorption. Steps 183-215 include all eight in-scope files of this verification, so the reconstruction discipline is scoped to exclude the very documents that mandate it -- compounded by Contradiction #8 (zero labels applied). Severity HIGH.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #13 — The scope of the derivation phase disagrees between Step 212 and Step 215
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 212 Section 212.5 states 'Steps 1-211 have largely been derivation'; Step 215 Section 215.31 and five other occurrences scope the reconstruction to S_1...S_182. The corpus states the derivation ran to 211 while scoping reconstruction to 182; the 29-step remainder is never reconciled, and 182 is never justified anywhere. Severity MEDIUM.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #14 — Subtraction on an undefined information measure, forbidden in Step 208 and performed anyway in Step 212
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 208 Section 208.10 writes L(C)=I_required-I_preserved and immediately cautions 'we should not treat this as a literal numeric quantity until we define an information measure.' Step 212 Section 212.19 writes L(C)=InformationBefore(C)-InformationAfter(C) without that caveat and without citing 208.10 -- no information measure is defined anywhere in the intervening four files. This is the fourth occurrence of the pattern in the band (208.3's I(A)<I(E), 208.10, 212.19, and 214.7's SemanticLoss(A)>0). Severity MEDIUM-HIGH.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #15 — Total order on epistemic strength declined in Step 209 Section 209.21 and then used in 209.25 and 210.9
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 209 Section 209.21 states Unknown≺Hypothesized≺Supported and explicitly declines a universal total ordering ('the actual epistemic lattice must be derived from the domain'). Step 209 Section 209.25 (S(T(x))>S(x)) and Step 210 Section 210.9 (Strength(T(x))>Strength(x)) both then use strict > on the same kind of quantity, presupposing the order that was just declined four sections earlier and never derived. Severity MEDIUM.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #16 — Invariants modeled as a dependency graph and as a flat conjunction, consecutively, within Step 209
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 209 Section 209.31 states that some invariants depend on others (HistoricalTraceability depends on Identity+Versioning+Provenance), illustrated with a 24-line ASCII dependency graph. Step 209 Section 209.32 then composes all invariants as a flat, order-free conjunction I_global=AND_{i=1}^n I_i. A conjunction cannot express dependency; the two sections model the same invariant set with incompatible structures, consecutively. Severity MEDIUM.

b_rows_sample.anchor: MATCH VERDICT: 6 of 8 agenda items delivered; 2 named and NOT delivered
b_rows_sample.statement: Probe (a): Step 207's tail agenda for Step 208 lists eight items (contract composition, information preservation, semantic loss, version compatibility, monotonicity, contradiction, uncertainty propagation, provenance preservation) under the question 'can a chain of individually valid transformations produce an invalid or misleading conclusion?'. Step 208 delivers 6 of 8: version compatibility is NOT delivered (Version appears only as a tuple field; no compatibility relation between contract versions is defined) and uncertainty propagation is NOT delivered (Section 208.14 shows uncertainty being lost, but no composition rule for uncertainty through C_2 o C_1 is given, and the word 'propagation' never occurs in Step 208). Additionally the headline question is restated, not quoted: 207 asks about an 'invalid or misleading conclusion'; 208 asks only whether the chain is 'necessarily valid' -- 'misleading' is dropped entirely and never addressed as distinct from invalidity.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Step 208 neither cites nor consumes Step 82 (Uncertainty Propagation)
b_rows_sample.statement: The corpus already contains a dedicated prior step, '# Step 82 — Uncertainty Propagation', whose own Section 1 states 'we now test whether our mathematical model remains correct when uncertainty passes through multiple layers' -- exactly the agenda item Step 207 assigned to Step 208. Step 208 both omits the item (uncertainty propagation) and omits the prior work that already addressed it, with zero citation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Answered from scratch: zero citations to Steps 048/050/058
b_rows_sample.statement: Probe (b): machine grep of Step 208 (and all 8 in-scope files) for the prior corpus's answers to the same headline question -- Step 048's boxed 'LocalCorrectness ⇏ GlobalCorrectness', Step 058's boxed 'CorrectContexts ⇏ CorrectComposition', and Step 050's Attack 5 ('semantic collision', PASS) -- finds zero matches anywhere in the band. Step 208 Section 208.13 re-derives the same proposition in new notation ('locally valid but globally invalid'), so the same proposition is now boxed four times in the corpus in four notations with zero cross-reference; under LATER != SUPERSEDING, Step 208 does not supersede 048 or 058, it duplicates them without knowing they exist. Step 208's Section 208.22 (contradiction propagation) and Section 208.15 (RichEvidence -> SimpleBoolean) likewise re-derive the ground of Step 050's Attack 2 and Attack 5 respectively, also uncited.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Further arithmetic checks: 0.87>=0.80 correct; 0.91+/-0.08 within range at 1 sigma but 2-sigma bound exceeds 1; ratio checks disclaimed
b_rows_sample.statement: Additional independently-verified arithmetic in the band: Step 209 Section 209.15's 0.87 >= 0.80 evaluates to True (correct). Step 208 Section 208.14 / Step 210 Section 210.12's 0.91 +/- 0.08 gives [0.83, 0.99], within [0,1] at 1-sigma, but at 2-sigma the upper bound is 1.07 > 1 -- out of range for a quantity called 'confidence', though the corpus never commits this specific error since the interval's coverage level is left unlabelled. Step 215 Section 215.24's ratios (182/43=4.233, 43/17=2.529, 17/8=2.125, 8/4=2.0, total 45.5x) make no arithmetic claim and are correctly disclaimed as unknown. Step 209 Section 209.42 vs Step 210 Section 210.25: |I_KOS|=8 vs |{I1..I15}|=15, difference 7, mapping absent (unreconciled).

b_rows_sample.statement: Step 208 ('Semantic Contract Algebra') treats a DDD context contract as an information-preserving projection and defines: semantic sufficiency S_B ⊆ I(C(A)) relative to a receiving context's task; minimal sufficient contract; semantic projection pi; semantic loss L(C) = I_required - I_preserved; semantic integrity SI(C,B); the anti-pattern 'Booleanization' (collapsing rich epistemic state into a Boolean); contract temporal validity C(t); provenance composition P(G)=P(A)∪P(E); the KnowledgeArtifact 6-tuple (Content, Meaning, Provenance, Validity, Version, EpistemicStatus); the Data->Information->Evidence->Assessment->KnowledgeClaim ladder; Proposition as a first-class object; and a four-layer architecture split (Epistemic/Normative/Decisional/Operational).

b_rows_sample.statement: Step 208 cites exactly one prior step by number (Step 207, 'we continue from...') and nothing else -- not Steps 048, 058, 050, or 082. b_rows_sample.anchor: EVOLUTION VERDICT: PARTIALLY_RESOLVES / REVIVES; DEFINITION VERDICT: PARTIALLY_CLEAR
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 208 resolves 6 of 8 of Step 207's agenda items and, unknowingly, revives already-boxed results from Steps 048 and 058. Definitionally: Booleanization, Suff(C,B,Task), semantic projection, and the four-layer split are CLEAR. The information measure I(.) is NOT DEFINED -- Section 208.3 writes an ordinal comparison I(A)<I(E) and Section 208.10 writes a difference L(C)=I_required-I_preserved while itself stating 'we should not treat this as a literal numeric quantity until we define an information measure' -- the measure is never defined and the operations are performed anyway. S_B ('the information necessary to perform its legitimate responsibility') is AMBIGUOUS because 'legitimate' is never defined, so S_B cannot be constructed for any concrete B.

b_rows_sample.anchor: FIRST INVALID INFERENCE: Section 208.3 (compounded at 208.10); SECOND DEFECT: Section 208.25's provenance equation
b_rows_sample.statement: DERIVATION VERDICT PARTIALLY_VALID. I(A)<I(E) presupposes a total order on information content; I_required-I_preserved presupposes an interval scale; neither is established (Section 208.10 explicitly declines to establish one, then uses the operations anyway) -- every downstream claim quantifying loss is conditional on repairing this. Second defect: P(G)=P(A)∪P(E), boxed as 'provenance must be closed under semantic transformation,' is either vacuous (if closure holds, P(A)∪P(E)=P(A)) or self-refuting (if it does not, provenance is not closed); it also excludes any provenance contributed by the governance act itself, directly conflicting with Step 209 Section 209.4's Final(D) ⇒ DecisionBasis(D) ∧ Authority(D) (see Contradiction #2).

b_rows_sample.anchor: COMPUTABILITY: nothing in Step 208 reaches CONSTRUCTIBLE; TEST VERDICT: NOT_EXECUTED
b_rows_sample.statement: Computability ladder for Step 208's objects: Booleanization is DEFINED; Semantic Sufficiency S_B⊆I(C(A)) is DEFINED but not INPUTS_KNOWN (both S_B and I uninstantiated); L(C) is DEFINED but explicitly barred from COMPUTABLE by its own Section 208.10; the Contract Safety theorem (Section 208.37) is DEFINED but not DERIVED. Nothing in the file reaches CONSTRUCTIBLE. Test verdict NOT_EXECUTED (0 tests specified, 0 run); the nine review questions in Section 208.38 are a checklist, not tests.

b_rows_sample.anchor: STATISTICAL VERDICT: STRONG on framing, WEAK on inference; MEASUREMENT VERDICT: FAILS on the information measure
b_rows_sample.statement: Statistically, Section 208.6's sufficient-statistic analogy is immediately and correctly fenced ('this is an analogy, not a claim that DDD contracts are literally sufficient statistics') but left un-cashed (no Fisher-Neyman factorization or formal criterion transposed), and Section 208.23's handling of conflicting estimates is sound but uncited against prior statistical steps (025N, 082). Measurement-wise: I(.) has no declared scale type yet is compared (<) and subtracted (-) -- arithmetic NOT justified; result=0.91 in one block silently becomes confidence=0.91 in the very next (unjustified type conversion between a point estimate and a degree of belief); uncertainty=0.08 is silently converted into a symmetric +/-0.08 interval half-width in Step 210 Section 210.12, presupposing an unstated symmetric error distribution and coverage level; epistemic strength S(x) is compared with > (Section 208.9 forward) while Step 209 Section 209.21 later explicitly retracts any universal total ordering on the same kind of quantity.

b_rows_sample.anchor: DDD VERDICT: STRONG — the best DDD content in the band; UBIQUITOUS-LANGUAGE: Evidence != Claim boxed, then violated two files later
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 208's sufficiency-relative-to-responsibility (Section 208.4) is a correct, non-obvious Published-Language/conformist-boundary formulation; S_B ⊆ I(C(A)) ≪ I(A) (Section 208.5) is precisely the anti-Shared-Kernel constraint; Booleanization (Section 208.16) is a genuinely useful named anti-pattern; the four-layer split (Section 208.36) is a defensible strategic decomposition -- but none of it is mapped to Step 206's bounded contexts or Step 207's actual context contracts. Section 208.28 rules 'we should not collapse [Data/Information/Evidence/Assessment/KnowledgeClaim] into one generic object called Knowledge' -- a ruling violated two files later (Contradiction #1). Section 208.30 promotes Proposition to a first-class term; Section 208.29 boxes Evidence != Claim but gives it no owning context ('term without an owner').

b_rows_sample.anchor: ASSUMPTIONS / HIDDEN ASSUMPTIONS; UNDEFINED SYMBOLS in Step 208
b_rows_sample.statement: Stated assumptions: a contract is total and deterministic; information is set-like so subset applies; S_B is knowable a priori. Hidden assumptions: that an information measure exists at all (Section 208.10 defers it and nothing in the band supplies one); that provenance sets are finite and mergeable (required by P(A)∪P(E), never stated); that Valid(C) (Section 208.2) and SI(C,B) (Section 208.12) are different predicates, though the text slides between them; that 'legitimate responsibility' (Section 208.4) is externally given, smuggling the governance model into the definition of sufficiency. Undefined symbols: I(.) (deferred), S_B (depends on undefined 'legitimate'), T_1, A_I/G_I/D_I, Preserve(.), RequiredProvenance(R_C), Knowledge(E).

b_rows_sample.anchor: WHAT SURVIVES / WHAT DOES NOT SURVIVE — Step 208
b_rows_sample.statement: Survives: Booleanization as a named anti-pattern; Suff(C,B,Task) (purpose-relative sufficiency); the four-layer split; Evidence != Claim; probability-of-proposition != truth-value-of-proposition; the explicit refusal to claim contracts are sufficient statistics; non-monotonicity as a requirement; the boxed claim 'the objective is not zero information loss, the objective is zero loss of relevant meaning' (the band's clearest and most durable architectural statement). Does not survive: L(C) as any quantity; I(A)<I(E) as a comparison; P(G)=P(A)∪P(E); the Section 208.37 'provisional architectural theorem' (Sufficiency+Provenance+Temporal Validity ⇒ Contract Safety), which is a definition dressed as an implication since Contract Safety is not independently defined -- not a theorem in any sense, a naming convention.

b_rows_sample.statement: Step 208 uses I exclusively for an information measure (I(E), I(A), I_required, I_preserved); Step 209 onward uses I exclusively for invariants (I_L, I_C, I_S, I_i, I_identity, I1-I15, I(s)). b_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #1 — Knowledge as a generic object: forbidden in 208, used as an Owner in 210
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 208 Section 208.28 boxes a prohibition: the Data->Information->Evidence->Assessment->KnowledgeClaim transformations of semantic status 'should not [be collapsed] into one generic object called Knowledge.' Step 210 Section 210.25's matrix row I11 nonetheless assigns Owner='Knowledge' (and row I3 compounds it with 'Knowledge infrastructure'), the exact generic object Step 208 boxed a prohibition against two files earlier in the same band. Severity HIGH; neither Step-206 bounded context, and neither file notices.

b_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #2 — Provenance composition (208) excludes the authority Step 209 requires
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 208 Section 208.25 asserts as an equality P(G)=P(A)∪P(E), boxed as 'provenance must be closed under semantic transformation.' Step 209 Section 209.4 requires Final(D)⇒DecisionBasis(D)∧Authority(D). Since Authority(D), the governance grant that made a decision final, is in neither P(A) nor P(E), a governed decision's provenance under Section 208.25 cannot contain its own authority, yet Step 209's own traceability requirement (Basis(D) including authority) demands that it does -- the two cannot both hold. Independently checked, the equality is additionally vacuous if closure holds (P(A)⊇P(E) implies the union is just P(A)) and self-refuting if it does not. Severity HIGH.

b_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #14 — Subtraction on an undefined information measure, forbidden in Step 208 and performed anyway in Step 212
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 208 Section 208.10 writes L(C)=I_required-I_preserved and immediately cautions 'we should not treat this as a literal numeric quantity until we define an information measure.' Step 212 Section 212.19 writes L(C)=InformationBefore(C)-InformationAfter(C) without that caveat and without citing 208.10 -- no information measure is defined anywhere in the intervening four files. This is the fourth occurrence of the pattern in the band (208.3's I(A)<I(E), 208.10, 212.19, and 214.7's SemanticLoss(A)>0). Severity MEDIUM-HIGH.

b_rows_sample.anchor: STEP 208 load-bearing boxed claims: Semantic Sufficiency, the provisional Contract-Safety theorem, and the survivor 'zero loss of relevant meaning'
b_rows_sample.statement: Three load-bearing boxed claims of Step 208, adjudicated: (1) 'Semantic Sufficiency: S_B⊆I(C(A))' -- the file's central definition, resting on the undefined I(.) and the undefined 'legitimate responsibility' in S_B. (2) 'Semantic Sufficiency + Provenance Preservation + Temporal Validity ⇒ Contract Safety' -- self-labelled 'a provisional architectural theorem, not a mathematically proven theorem'; verifier judges it a stipulative definition of Contract Safety rather than an implication, since the consequent is not independently defined. (3) 'The objective is not zero information loss. The objective is zero loss of relevant meaning.' -- survives; the band's clearest and most durable architectural statement.

a_rows_sample.statement: Reframes Step 288's relationship to the pre-existing Step 261 stop-gate: Step 288 must consume Step 261 as a binding boundary condition, not supersede or re-decide it, and must not interpret Step 261's demand that kernel selection stop while equality remains ambiguous as license to declare equality fully solved; recommends retitling the mandate 'EQUALITY CONTRACT CLOSURE AND STEP-261 GATE REASSESSMENT' since a fully valid research outcome is 'equality contract partially closed; Step-261 kernel-selection gate remains blocked.'

The correct chain is: Step 261 stop-gate ↓ Step 287 boundary ↓ Step 288 equality-contract investigation ↓ derivable closure / bounded alternatives / normative decisions / technical gaps ↓ reassess Step-261 gate ↓ gate open (if justified) / gate remains blocked
a_rows_sample.statement: Names a specific logical fallacy to guard against ('we resolved one equality question, therefore equality is resolved, therefore kernel selection may proceed' -- not logically valid) and replaces it with the correct dependency chain: Step 261 stop-gate -> Step 287 boundary -> Step 288 equality-contract investigation (producing derivable closures, bounded alternatives, normative decisions, technical gaps) -> reassess the Step-261 gate -> either the gate opens (if justified) or it remains blocked.

b_rows_sample.anchor: `CORPUS` — **Step 261 §261.23** declines to declare `≡_K` final and lists six reasons, including *"the observation set is not fully closed"* and *"the operation registry is not fully closed"*, then: *"final kernel selection must stop while equality remains ambiguous. **We therefore obey that gate.**"*
b_rows_sample.statement: Corroboration is drawn from Step 261 §261.23, which already declines to declare state equality (≡_K) final, listing six reasons (including that the observation set and operation registry are not fully closed) and mandating that final kernel selection stop while equality remains ambiguous. This research programme is said to have reached the same stop-gate by its own independent route, before this programme existed; the equality gap is therefore not a new discovery of the current verification lane — what this pass newly adds is the per-relation decision-procedure audit plus the ≈_X and product-order narrowings.

b_rows_sample.anchor: STEP 261 GATE — MUST BE PRESERVED ... Step 288 MUST NOT declare final kernel selection closed merely because: - Π has been discussed; - X has been bounded; - identity has been clarified; - some equality procedures exist.
b_rows_sample.statement: Treats Step 261 section 261.23 as a binding stop-gate that Step 288 must consume, not override: explicitly forbids declaring kernel selection closed merely because Pi has been discussed, X has been bounded, identity has been clarified, or some equality procedures exist -- requiring instead a re-evaluation of every Step-261 closure condition in a table (condition / current status / evidence / does Step 288 resolve it / remaining dependency), with kernel selection remaining open if any condition remains open. (This precisely anticipates the later finding, in 05-STEP-261-GATE-AUDIT.md, that all four of these forbidden grounds for closure did occur in Step 288's results and none licensed closure.)

b_rows_sample.statement: Quotes Step 261.23's stop-gate verbatim in full: it declines to state equiv_K is final equality for six named reasons (observation set not fully closed; operation registry not fully closed; provenance placement unresolved; assertion semantics unresolved; temporal semantics unresolved; identity semantics unresolved), and the governing prompt explicitly requires final kernel selection to stop while equality remains ambiguous -- '261.28: FINAL KERNEL SELECTION REMAINS BLOCKED.'

b_rows_sample.statement: Re-audits all six of Step 261.23's closure conditions against Step 288's actual output: (1) observation set still open -- the bounded 32-projection Sigma-level family is not the closed 𝒪_K the corpus means; (2) operation registry still open -- global congruence unprovable (259) and 6 of 11 mandate operations unanalysed; (3) provenance placement sharpened not resolved -- decomposes into a technical part decidable by the 258-A congruence experiment plus a normative residue; (4) assertion semantics still open, entirely outside Step 288's scope, owned by a commissioned Step 262; (5) temporal semantics still open and arguably WORSENED, since equiv is shown to be a (context,time)-indexed family; (6) identity semantics narrowed by I_48 but still open (5 of 11 identity kinds absent, parameter unbound). b_rows_sample.statement: Re-evaluates 261.29's fourteen-row overall theory-readiness gate (operation set closed, operation signatures typed, state semantics defined, assertion type defined, status algebra defined, equality defined, identity defined, congruence proven, minimality proven, provenance placement resolved, computability established, implementation correspondence, empirical validation, remaining normative decisions), finding most rows unchanged from 261's own status, with a few genuinely improved from red to yellow (status algebra: Sigma axes enumerated and counted at 2240, though 0/5 orders established; equality and identity: qualitatively deepened by register reconciliation and I_48, though not defined), and one row actively worsened by execution (congruence: '=' is now disproven as a congruence, not merely unproven).

b_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly checks Step 288's own results against the mandate's four forbidden grounds for premature closure and finds all four literally occurred: Pi has been discussed (true, and not resolution); X has been bounded (true, exactly 32, executed -- but that bounds a Sigma-level family, not the corpus's 𝒪_K); identity has been clarified (true, via I_48 -- but 'identity context' remains undefined); some equality procedures exist (true, =, ≡_D, ~_F, ≈_X -- but none is a congruence and ~_F is explicitly insufficient). b_rows_sample.anchor: ## §16.5 `261.30`'s dependency chain, adopted verbatim ... **Step 288 operates at links 3–5 only.** ... $$\boxed{\text{Equality is a family of semantic relations, not necessarily a single primitive.}}$$
b_rows_sample.statement: Adopts 261.30's six-link dependency chain verbatim (Ontology -> State Representation -> Identity -> Equality -> Congruence -> Minimality, with epistemic status/provenance/temporal validity/external context noted by 261.30 as interacting with the chain rather than sitting linearly inside it) and observes Step 288 operates only at links 3-5 (Identity, Equality, Congruence); links 1-2 (Ontology, State Representation) are upstream and entirely unresolved, so even a fully-closed equality would not by itself close the chain. b_rows_sample.anchor: $$\boxed{\textbf{YES — and Step 289 STRENGTHENS the gate rather than merely inheriting it.}}$$ **Three independent grounds** ... 1. **The gate's own criterion is met by measurement.** ... 2. **A new ground `261` did not have:** the `≡`/`≈` **definitional conflict** ... 3. **A second new ground:** `=` ... **EXECUTED not a congruence**
b_rows_sample.statement: Concludes 261.23 still legitimately stops kernel selection, on three independent grounds none of which is mere deference to age: (1) the gate's own criterion (stop while equality is ambiguous) is directly met by the computed minimal cut {equiv} -- confirmed by a method the original Step 261 never used; (2) a genuinely new ground unavailable to 261 -- the equiv/approx definitional conflict, meaning two of the six state-level relations cannot both stand as written, so selecting a kernel over a self-contradictory equality register would mean selecting over an undefined term; (3) a second new ground -- structural equality ('='), the one relation everyone treated as trivially available, is now EXECUTED-disproven as a congruence and decidable only relative to a canonicalization the corpus forbids fixing a priori.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ## ⚠️ Where the gate is now over-broad — and this cuts the other way ... **Conditions 4 and 5 do not block *equality*; they block *kernel selection* for separate reasons.** ... **All six remain unresolved; the gate holds. What changes is that it is now known to be a conjunction of two independent blocks, not one.**
b_rows_sample.statement: Offers a structural critique of the gate itself: 261.23's six conditions are not equally load-bearing -- equiv sits in the actual feedback structure (all 4 cycles), O/T/O_K are hard upstream blockers but not cycle members, provenance placement (condition 3) is downstream of equiv via Pi->equiv rather than an independent blocker, while assertion semantics (condition 4) and temporal semantics (condition 5) are ORTHOGONAL to equality entirely, blocking kernel selection for separate reasons. Warns that bundling all six under one gate labelled 'while equality remains ambiguous' conflates two independent blocks and could mislead a future step into believing that resolving equality would release conditions 4-5 -- it would not. Explicitly frames this as a refinement of the gate's internal structure, not a proposal to release any part of it: all six conditions remain unresolved and the gate holds as a conjunction of an equality block (conditions 1,2,3,6) and a separate representation block (conditions 4,5).

b_rows_sample.anchor: $$\boxed{\textbf{NO — not one of the six.}}$$ ... **The two-block structure from Step 289 §5 is reconfirmed, unchanged:** **equality block = conditions 1, 2, 3, 6 · representation block = conditions 4, 5.**
b_rows_sample.statement: Confirms adjudicating equiv-vs-approx satisfies NONE of Step 261.23's six closure conditions individually: condition 1 (observation set) is untouched since N-1A merely classifies the register without closing O_K; condition 2 (operation registry) is untouched (that is N-4's territory); condition 3 (provenance placement) is untouched (that is Decision 3/N-2); conditions 4 and 5 (assertion/temporal semantics) are entirely orthogonal to equality; condition 6 (identity semantics) was already narrowed earlier by I_48, and N-1 adds nothing further to it. Reconfirms Step 289's two-block gate structure (equality block = conditions 1,2,3,6; representation block = conditions 4,5) unchanged.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Steps 288–289 had added a **seventh** ground for the gate: *"the register is self-contradictory, so selecting a kernel would be selecting over an undefined term."* **That ground is withdrawn.** ... | the six `261.23` conditions | ✅ **all six intact, 0 of 6 resolved** | | `{≡}` is the unique minimal cycle cut | ✅ **intact** | | `=` is not a congruence ... | ✅ **intact** | ~~the `≡`/`≈` corpus contradiction~~ | 🔴 **WITHDRAWN** | ⚠️ **The gate does not weaken.**
b_rows_sample.statement: Formally withdraws a seventh ground that Steps 288-289 had added to the Step-261 stop-gate ('the equiv/approx register is self-contradictory, so selecting a kernel would mean selecting over an undefined term'), replacing it with N-1A's finding that the register is a well-formed (if incomplete) typed family, not a contradiction. States explicitly that the gate does not thereby weaken: it still rests on all six original 261.23 conditions (0 of 6 resolved), plus two grounds independently established by Step 289 ({equiv} being the unique minimal cycle cut, and structural equality being executed-disproven as a congruence and canonicalization-conditional) -- removing an over-stated ground from a conclusion that has other sufficient grounds leaves the conclusion standing and the reasoning more honest, not weaker; reporting the withdrawal itself as a weakening would be exactly as wrong as the original overclaim.

b_rows_sample.anchor: **Resolving equality would NOT close the `261.23` gate** — conditions 4 and 5 are a separate block. **And `N-1` does not resolve equality** — it resolves only whether the register is self-contradictory. **Two levels of "not enough", and neither should be collapsed into the other.**
b_rows_sample.statement: Issues an explicit anti-misreading warning distinguishing two separate 'not enough' levels that must not be collapsed into one another: even a fully resolved equality would not by itself close the 261.23 gate (conditions 4 and 5 form an independent representation block), and separately, N-1 does not resolve equality at all -- it resolves only whether the equality/observational register is internally self-contradictory (which it is not).

b_rows_sample.anchor: `258.9`: "For every valid transformation `T ∈ 𝒯` we require `K_1 ≡_K K_2 ⇒ T(K_1,c) ≡_K T(K_2,c)` for all admissible common contexts `c`. This is the critical mathematical requirement. If it fails, then `≡_K` is too coarse."
b_rows_sample.statement: The corpus's requirement that operations respect the semantic equality relation (congruence) is stated over ≡_K and the transformation family alone, with no mention of the observational relation approx, giving congruence an independent evidentiary basis separate from equality-vs-observational-equivalence questions.

b_rows_sample.statement: Status summary: congruence's independent basis is ESTABLISHED; global congruence itself remains TECHNICALLY OPEN and BLOCKED on the transformation family T and transition semantics delta.

b_rows_sample.anchor: G-76 | `261` carries one relation register in two notations, and the second reuses the `≡` glyph for `≡_H`/`≡_P` — so `≡` appears to do four jobs. A plausible cause of `G-67`'s misreading
b_rows_sample.statement: New documentary gap G-76: Step 261 states the same six-relation register in two different notations (261.1 and 261.20/261.25), with the second notation overloading the equiv/congruence glyph across four different relation roles, plausibly explaining why the equiv/approx 'contradiction' was mis-detected.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 0 RESOLVED · 2 PARTIAL · 4 FAILED
b_rows_sample.statement: Re-derives, condition by condition with cited evidence, that of Step 261's six stop-gate conditions, zero are RESOLVED, two are PARTIAL (3: provenance placement - method exists but residual is normative; 6: identity - one real narrowing via I_48 but identity context undefined), and four are FAILED (1: observation closure; 2: operation closure, narrower than reported - a membership rule is missing, not an enumeration; 4: assertion semantics; 5: temporal semantics).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Conditions 4 and 5 have not moved in any of Steps 287–291. They are orthogonal to the entire equality programme. Five steps of equality work have not touched them, which is itself the evidence that they are a separate block
b_rows_sample.statement: Reconfirms, for a third time across the programme, that 261.23's six conditions split into an equality block (1,2,3,6) and a representation block (4,5); the fact that five consecutive steps of intensive equality research have produced zero movement on conditions 4-5 is treated as itself the evidence that they are structurally separate and will not be released by resolving equality.
